by: row 43, in a volume opened to look for somebody else
what: GENERATION FOUR HAD NO HOUSEHOLD IN THIS ARCHIVE — and its earliest child is now documented, from an act that proves an unsourced tree claim
was: **RAFFAELE FALCO** (b. 10 May 1818) married **ANGELA ROSA MORGILLO** (b. San Felice a Cancello, 24 February 1818) in **1844**, and this archive held **no household for them**. Raffaele appeared only as a child inside his father's house, and their first documented child was **generation five's CARMINE ANTONIO FALCO, born 10 July 1850**. The family tree named a daughter **VINCENZA FALCO**, unsourced.
now:
**Act 92 of the 1847 Arienzo birth register**: «*il dì **VENTUNO** del mese di **NOVEMBRE** … è comparso **RAFFAELE FALCO, di anni TRENTA**, di professione **CONTADINO**, domiciliato **in strada CAMELLARA** … nata da **ANGELA ROSA MORGILLO sua moglie legittima, di anni VENTINOVE** … nel giorno **VENTI** del mese di **NOVEMBRE** … **alle ore VENTUNO, nella casa sua propria** … il nome di **VINCENZA***». The parish notice, returned the same day, names her «**VINCENZA FALCO**».

**The household «Raffaele Falco & Angela Rosa Morgillo» now exists**, with Vincenza as its earliest child — **two years and eight months older than generation five**.
how: The 1847 birth register was read end to end at the **parents band** while hunting a child of a different household for work-list row 43.
why:
**A TREE ASSERTION BECAME A DOCUMENT.** This archive marks everything from the family tree «*unverified unless a document says so*». **Here is the document**, and it agrees with the tree on the name, the father and the mother.

**And both stated ages are exact** — thirty against a birth of 10 May 1818, twenty-nine against 24 February 1818 — **in an office this archive has repeatedly shown guessing ages by five years**. Two exact readings in one act is rare enough to be worth saying.

**She is named for her paternal grandfather, VINCENZO FALCO**, who was living on the same street.

**THREE WOMEN OF THIS NAME, AND ONLY THIS ONE IS DOCUMENTED FROM HER OWN BIRTH.** A **VINCENZA FALCO, one day old**, died on strada Camellara in 1820; a **VINCENZA FALCO «fu Matteo»** is the wife of **CARMINE MORGILLO** in the 1870s extracts. *This town keeps proving that a name identifies nobody.*

**The find is a by-product.** The volume was opened for **GIUSEPPE FALCO**, a child of Crescenzo Falco — **who is not in it**. *Reading a year out for one household is how the archive finds the others.*

by: row 43 — and the archive's own notes had two of these children for days
what: CRESCENZO FALCO AND ANGELA MARIA MORGILLO HAVE FOUR CHILDREN — and the household that had none held one act that could not be theirs
was: **A household created on 3 February 1845 and completely unexamined.** Its only member was «*Joseph Falco filius **Crescentii** et **Mariae Morgillo**, aetate paucorum dierum*», a parish burial dated here **1818** — **the year before the husband was born.** Work-list row 43 had swept 1846 and the last two months of 1845 on the declarant line and found no Crescenzo.
now:
**Four children, three of them read from the image today.**

**MARIA FELICE FALCO, born 21 November 1845** (Nati 1845 act 111) — «*è comparso **CRESCENZO FALCO, di anni VENTICINQUE**, di professione contadino, domiciliato in questo comune **STRADA CAMELLARA** … nata da **MARIA MORGILLO** sua moglie legittima, di anni **VENTITRE***». **And the margin of her act carries her wedding**: «*A **3 Febbrajo 1873** l'Uff.e dello Stato Civ.e d'ARIENZO sposò **MARIA FELICE FALCO** con **PASQUALE QUOTOLO*** — Caserta 18 Giugno 1884».

**GIUSEPPE FALCO**, dead **2 June 1848**, **aged one**, and **GENNARO FALCO**, born **1 June 1848** (Nati 1848 act 42) and dead **3 June 1848** at **two days**. **Brothers, dead a day apart, in one house on strada Camellara**, both declared by the same two neighbours.
how: The 1845 register was re-swept at the **PARENTS band**; the 1848 birth register was swept the same way and gave act 42; the two death acts were opened at the image.
why:
**THE HOUSEHOLD WAS NEVER TWO HOUSEHOLDS.** «*Crescenzo Falco × **MARIA** Morgillo*» and «*Crescenzo Falco & **ANGELA MARIA** Morgillo*» are one couple: **the marriage act calls her Angela Maria and every birth and death act of her children calls her plain Maria**, at twenty-three in 1845 and twenty-five in 1848 — the age she was when she married. *So the family tree's unsourced «Maria Concetta Morgillo» is most likely this woman under a third form of her name.*

**THE DATE WAS THE WHOLE PROBLEM.** The parish burial is **1848**, not 1818: the civil act of 2 June 1848 names the same child, the same parents and the same street, and **the first weeks of January 1818 and January 1848 were both read to test it — neither holds a Falco infant.** *The parish page's other entries run across the 1840s and 1850s; the OCR had turned «1848 … 2 Ju[nii]» into «1818 … 2 Ja[nuarii]».*

**AND THE ARCHIVE HAD TWO OF THESE CHILDREN ALREADY.** `notes/1844-1847-death-indexes.md` records both 1848 deaths, read from the image in an earlier session, under the heading «**CRESCENZO FALCO × MARIA MORGILLO is a household this archive has never held**». **It is this one.** The note was written before the birth act that names her Maria, and it went into no data file. *That is «harvesting is not holding», and it cost row 43 a week.*

**Row 43's own sweep could not have found them.** It read the **declarant line**; Maria Felice's act is at images **116–117** and the sweep began at **118**, and Gennaro's act was presented by a **midwife**, whose name is the only one on that line.

by: row 86 — the second «no Falco» overturned in one day
what: 1817 was published as «No Falco» and holds TWO — and one of them was already cited in this archive's own household file
was: **«No Falco. But two Arcangelo Crisci, aged 52 and 30, declaring births in the same year … All 77 fathers read are logged with age, trade and street.»** Outcome: **no Falco**.
now:
**Act 49, 15 May 1817 — SALVATORE DIGLIO**, to **ALFONSO DIGLIO, twenty-eight, of strada CAMELLARA**, and **MARIA FALCO, twenty-seven**. **New.**

**Act 69, 22 September 1817 — GIOVANNA MORGILLO**, to **CARLANTONIO MORGILLO** and **ROSA FALCO** — **a daughter of the founders MATTEO FALCO and FRANCESCA CRISCI**. **This act is cited in this archive's own households file, at this very volume, image 36 left.**
how: The 1817 register was read act by act for work-list row 86, at the combined band its prose format allows — declarant and mother on one half-page.
why:
**The row says «all 77 fathers read are logged with age, trade and street», and Alfonso Diglio is one of them.** He is a DIGLIO. **The reading that failed was of the MOTHER's line**, which in this format sits three lines below the father's — and it is where every Falco woman in this archive is found.

**And the second act needed no reading at all.** Giovanna Morgillo's birth, of **ROSA FALCO**, has been cited here with this volume's ark and image number since before this week. **The coverage page and the household file have been contradicting each other about this year**, and the coverage page is the one a reader trusts to say «do not look again».

**That is the second «no Falco» overturned today**, after 1838. **Both were the strongest negative this archive publishes, and both were produced by reading one band of a two-band act.** See work-list row 86.

what: THE REGISTER RECORDS ONE OF ITS OWN ERRORS — a mother's surname wrong in a birth act, corrected by a court order nineteen years later
was: This archive reads its women out of one line of a birth act — «*e da **MARIA FALCO** sua moglie legittima*», «*da **ANDREANA CRISCI** sua moglie legittima*» — and treats the reading problem as one of **handwriting**: a long ſ against a t, an r shoulder against none. **That the clerk might have written the wrong surname altogether has been a possibility, not a documented fact.**
now: **It is documented.** Image 59 of the 1819 Arienzo birth register carries a *notamento* of **4 January 1839**: «*Si nota che con deliberazione del Tribunale … di questa Provincia del dì **ventiuno** dell'or caduto mese di **Dicembre**, ed anno mille ottocento **trentotto**, essendosi ordinata la **rettifica dell'errore d'incorso nell'atto di nascita di ANGELA ROSA COSSI** seguita in questo Comune nel giorno **quindici** del mese di **Novembre** dell'anno mille ottocento **diciannove**, descritto sotto il numero d'ordine **CENTOQUATTORDICI** del presente registro, spiegandosi di esser costei **nata da ANGELO COSSI, e da PAOLA BELELLA, e non già da PAOLA VERDICCHIO come sta scritto in esso***».
how: Found while reading the 1819 volume act by act for work-list row 86.
why:
**BELELLA and VERDICCHIO are not a palaeography problem.** They share no letters, no length and no shape. **The clerk simply wrote the wrong woman's surname into the act**, and it stood for nineteen years until a court ordered it corrected and the *sindaco* entered the order in the margin of the register.

**So the mother's line of an Arienzo birth act is not merely hard to read — it can be wrong.** That is a different kind of doubt from the one this archive has been managing, and it cannot be magnified away.

**No Falco act is placed under suspicion by this.** It is published because the possibility is now a documented fact of this register rather than an abstraction, and because **the correction mechanism is itself useful**: a *rettifica* leaves a dated note on the original leaf, which means **any act this archive reads may carry one**, and a margin is the first thing to look at.

by: reading the 1819 register for row 86, and checking the find against what was already held
what: Strada Camellara stopped telling the two Giuseppe Falco apart in 1819, not 1823 — and the archive held the act that proves it
was: «*So from **1823** the street no longer tells this Giuseppe Falco from the Giuseppe Falco who married Antonia di Guida. This archive leans on strada Camellara constantly; it stopped being a discriminator in **1823**.*» — published in two places, on the household page and in work-list row 58.
now: **1819.** Act 33 of the 1819 birth register, **18 March**: «*è comparso **GIUSEPPE FALCO**, di anni **TRENTOTTO**, di professione **MASSARO DI CAMPAGNA**, domiciliato in detto comune **strada CAMELLARA** … e da **GELSOMINA VIGLIOTTA** sua moglie legittima, d'anni **TRENTACINQUE***». **Seven months later the other Giuseppe Falco — a *contadino*, married to Antonia di Guida — declares a birth on the same street.**
how: The 1819 register was opened for work-list row 86, and the act was checked against the archive before anything was claimed.
why:
**The act was already here.** It sits on this household's own page, read from the image, with a note that says in so many words «*this archive has the household at STRADA COSTA in 1816. Either they moved, or the street is not the identifier here.*» **Two rows of one household disagreed by four years about when this archive's most-used discriminator failed**, and the wrong one is the one the prose repeats.

**And the check that caught it is the one that matters.** The 1819 act looked like a new find — a Falco on the wrong street, four years early. **Checking it against what was already held turned a false correction into a real one.** A find announced as new that the archive already holds is the mirror of a missed correction, and it is the more embarrassing of the two.

by: rows 35 and 86, reading the 1825 volume end to end
what: Clementina Diglio's birth is ACT 62, not act 72 — and the register's own order proves it without reading a letter
was: **CLEMENTINA DIGLIO, born 30 May 1825** to **ALFONSO DIGLIO** and **MARIA FALCO** of strada Camellara, cited here as «**atto 72**, folio 321, img 65r-66l».
now: **ACT 62.** The heading reads «*Num. d'ordine **SESSANTADUE***» in both of its columns.
how: The 1825 birth register was read end to end for the first time, and the act numbers of images 62 to 70 were swept as a block.
why:
**The handwriting did not have to be trusted.** Images 62 to 70 carry acts **59, 60, 61, 62, 63, 64, 65, 66, 67** and folios **318 to 326** — an unbroken run. **Folio 321, which this citation already carried, belongs to act 62.** The register's own order settles it, as it settled the December-1814 marriage earlier this week.

**«Sessantadue» and «settantadue» differ by one stroke in this hand** — a doubled long ſſ against a doubled tt — and that is exactly the kind of word this archive has learned not to decide by eye. *A three-letter difference carried an act number for months.*

*The rest of the citation was right, including the folio and both image numbers.*

by: rows 35 and 86, and a death act read for the first time
what: There are THREE Giuseppe Cioffi in this household, not two — and the death this archive held under the neighbour who declared it belongs to the second
was:
**GIUSEPPE CIOFFI «the second»**, born 5 October 1829 and probably the child dead 5 December 1830 at fourteen months. The household held **one** earlier Giuseppe, dead 25 March 1824 aged five.

And a third act sat elsewhere entirely: on 2 May 1827 **GIUSEPPE FALCO** declared, as «*vicino del defunto*», the death of a **GIUSEPPE CIOFFI aged one, son of FRANCESCO CIOFFI**. **It was filed under Giuseppe Falco, the declarant, and never under the child's own household.**
now: **Three Giuseppe Cioffi, in order.** The **first**, dead 25 March 1824 aged five, born about 1819. The **second**, born **9 March 1826** (act 19) and dead **1 May 1827** at one year old. The **third**, born 5 October 1829 (act 74) and probably dead 5 December 1830. **The child this archive called «the second» is the third.**
how: The 1826 birth register was read for the first time and gave act 19; the 1827 death act, cited here since before this week, was then opened at the image to see whether it was the same child.
why:
**The death act names the MOTHER, and that is what settles it**: «*figlio di **FRANCESCO CIOFFI**, di professione contadino, domiciliato ivi, **e di MARIA FALCO**, domiciliata ivi*». **Francesco Cioffi is not a name that identifies anybody at Arienzo** — this archive holds another one married to Crescenza Crisci — so a death act naming only the father could not have been joined to this household at all. **One line of the act does the whole job.**

**And the act had been harvested without being held.** It was in the archive as a sentence about **Giuseppe Falco**, who declared it as a neighbour; **the household whose child died did not carry it.** That is the failure this archive has named before as *harvesting is not holding*, and it hid a death for months in plain sight.

*Two smaller things from the same reading: the act is dated **2 May 1827**, not 1 May, which is the day of the death; and the clerk again separates his two declarants in one sentence — Giuseppe Falco «vicino del defunto», **CESARE CIOFFI «parente del defunto»**.*

by: rows 35 and 86, reading a volume that had only ever been indexed
what: Maddalena Falco's birth is ACT 57, not act 52 — the number came from the index and the index was misread
was: **MADDALENA FALCO (the second), born 4 May 1827**, stood here on the authority of the 1827 *tavola alfabetica* alone, with the note «*the act itself (atto 52) has not been read*» and **no street at all**.
now: **ACT 57**, read from the image. The heading says **«Num. d'ordine CINQUANTASETTE»** in both of its columns, and the acts on the leaves either side are **56** and **58**. The act adds what the index could not: the birth is on **strada CAMELLARA**, at **eleven in the morning**, «*nella casa d'abitazione di detti conjugi*»; her father is **GIUSEPPE FALCO, forty-five, COLONO** and her mother **ANTONIA DI GUIDO, forty**; the witnesses are **GENNARO LETTIERI, thirty-two, of strada Costa**, and **RAFFAELE COSSI**.
how: The 1827 birth register was read end to end at both bands for the first time, and the act was opened at the image the act-number sweep pointed to.
why:
**The index is not the act, and this archive has now been caught by that twice in one week.** A *tavola* is contemporaneous and in the registrar's hand, which is why it is trusted for a name and a date — but its act numbers are copied, and a copied numeral is exactly the sort of thing that goes wrong.

**The row said so itself.** It carried «*the act itself (atto 52) has not been read*», which is the honest hedge working as intended: the claim was labelled, and reading it cost one leaf. **What the hedge could not prevent was the number being cited as though it were read.**

**And a volume that has only been indexed is not a volume that has been read.** The 1827 register had never been opened at all before today; the 1826 register had been opened at one page. Between them they gave **three findings the index could never have produced**, because a tavola indexes the CHILD's surname and this family's Falco women are indexed under their husbands'.

by: row 85, on the last volume on its list
what: A YEAR PUBLISHED AS «NO FALCO AT ALL» HOLDS TWO FALCO BIRTHS — and one is STANISLAO FALCO, a son of generation three
was: **«NO FALCO AT ALL, AND NO CRISCI. Vincenzo Falco and Andreana Crisci have no child registered at Arienzo in 1838.»** That is what this archive published of the 1838 Arienzo birth register, after reading it end to end at the parents band, and the row's outcome was set to **no Falco** — the strongest negative this coverage register has.
now:
**The year holds two Falco births.**

**Act 79, 9 September 1838: STANISLAO FALCO**, «*è comparso **VINCENZO FALCO, di anni QUARANTASEI, di professione CONTADINO, domiciliato in strada CAMELLARA** … nato da **ANDREANA CRISCI sua moglie legittima, di anni QUARANTA** … **nella casa sua propria d'abitazione** … il nome di **STANISLAO***». **This archive had him only from his wedding of 1861.**

**Act 77, 4 September 1838: MARINO ALESSANDRO FALCO**, to **MICHELANGELO FALCO, thirty-four**, and **MARIA MIGLIORE, thirty-five**, of **strada SANT'ANDREA** — a Falco this archive did not have at all, and **a third wife for Michelangelo Falco in seven years**.
how: Sweeping the **declarant band** — `--band 0.34 0.19 --half R` — across a volume already read end to end at the parents band, for work-list row 85.
why:
**Both acts fail in exactly the place row 85 predicted, and the old entry contains the proof of it.** Each left-hand page — the one this archive reads for parents — says «*è nato da [the mother] sua moglie legittima … **E DA LUI DICHIARANTE**, di anni come sopra, di professione come sopra, domiciliato come sopra*». **The father's name is not written there.** So the parents band read **ANDREANA CRISCI** and **MARIA MIGLIORE** and found no Falco.

**The row even reported «no Crisci» — and Andreana Crisci is named in full on the left page of act 79.** A band that cannot see a surname cannot be trusted to have seen the one beside it either.

**This is the most expensive kind of error this archive can make**, and the reason row 85 exists: **a negative is the one result nobody re-checks**. «No Falco» is an instruction to stop looking. It stood over a son of generation three whose birth act had never been found.

**Six other years were re-read at the second band the same day** — 1821, 1822, 1823, 1829, 1832, 1833 — and between them the band has now produced **ROSARIA FALCO (1821)**, **MARIA CARMELA FALCO (1832)**, **STANISLAO FALCO (1838)** and **MARINO ALESSANDRO FALCO (1838)**, three of the four in households this archive already had. **Every one of those years had been published as read.**

by: row 85, the second band — and this time on the direct line
what: A DAUGHTER OF GENERATION THREE THE ARCHIVE HAD PUBLISHED AS NOT EXISTING — MARIA CARMELA FALCO, 10 October 1832
was: **«Vincenzo Falco and Andreana Crisci have no child in 1832 — the second of the two years where one fits their sibling spacing, and both are now spent.»** That is what this archive published after reading the whole 1832 birth register at the parents band. Their children were held as running **1830 → 1834** with nothing between.
now:
**ACT 84 of 1832, read from the image on 21 September 2026.** «*L'anno mille ottocento **TRENTADUE**, il dì **DIECI** del mese di **OTTOBRE**, ad ore **QUINDICI** … è comparso **VINCENZO FALCO, di anni QUARANTA, di professione CONTADINO, domiciliato ivi, strada CAMELLARA**, quale ci ha presentato una **FEMINA** … nata da **ANDREANA CRISCI sua moglie legittima, di anni TRENTASEI** … **alle ore DODICI, nella casa sua propria** … il nome di **MARIA CARMELA***».

**A daughter of generation three, born in her father's own house on strada Camellara**, baptised at Sant'Andrea the same day, witnessed by **PIETRO MAURO, twenty-three, *sartore*** and **FILIPPO GIGLIO, twenty-six**.
how: Sweeping the **declarant band** — `--band 0.34 0.19 --half R` — across a volume that had already been read end to end the other way.
why:
**The act says, in so many words, why the first reading could not find her.** The left-hand page of the opening, which is where this archive reads parents, says «*nata da **ANDREANA CRISCI** sua moglie legittima … **E DA LUI DICHIARANTE**, di anni come sopra, di professione come sopra, domiciliato come sopra*». **The father's name is not on that page at all.** A parents-band sweep sees a Crisci, no Falco, and moves on. **That is precisely the gap work-list row 85 was raised to describe — and it had cost this line a child of its own.**

**Nor could any index have rescued it.** The 1832 *tavola alfabetica* exists and is filled, and **it stops at C** — eighteen entries for a hundred and ten acts, with the leaf's verso not filmed. **There is no F column for 1832.** The two bands are the only instruments there are.

**Two details worth keeping.** First, **both parents' stated ages are exactly right** — forty against a baptism of 1 February 1792, thirty-six against 30 November 1796 — in an archive that has published, with demonstrations, that these clerks guessed ages by up to five years. Second, **she is NOT the other Maria Carmela Falco of 1832**, born 15 July on the same street to Francescantonio Falco and Maria Raffaela Falco. Two girls of one name and one surname on one street, twelve weeks apart, in a town where the name identifies nobody.

**What it does not settle.** Her act carries **no marginal annotation**, so no later marriage is recorded on it, and what became of her is open. And she is **not Nunziata Falco**: the sibling-spacing argument that made 1832 a candidate year is now answered by a different child, and Nunziata's birth is still in no Arienzo register.

by: row 85, caught by re-reading a volume it had asked for
what: Work-list row 85 asked for a volume that was already done, and the tool built to catch exactly that could not see it
was: Row 85 listed **1831** among the birth registers «*still owed a second band*». On that instruction the 1831 register was swept again at the declarant band — **a hundred images, for the third time**.
now: **1831 had already been read at BOTH bands, and the coverage page said so in its first sentence**: «*RE-READ at the PARENTS band; the earlier pass swept the DECLARANT line*». The years genuinely owed a second band are **1832, 1833, 1837 and 1838** — 1820 is exempt, and 1821, 1822, 1823 and 1829 are now done.
how: The reading itself found the error: opening the coverage row to write the null into it showed the null was already there.
why:
**`tools/staleness_report.py` was written to print this exact pair** — an open work-list row asking for a year and a series the coverage register records as read. **It printed nothing.** Its trigger phrases were «still to try», «still to read», «remains», «not read», «never read», «unread», «next» — and row 85 says «**still owed a second band**» and «**Remaining:**». *«Remaining» is not «remains»*: the pattern ends in a word boundary the word's own «i» defeats.

**A missing trigger word is indistinguishable from a clean report.** The tool failed toward silence, which is the direction a check must never fail in — a noisy false hit gets looked at, a silent miss gets believed. The triggers now include *still owed*, *owed a*, *remaining*, *yet to* and *outstanding*, and the tool finds the row.

**The re-reading is published as a null rather than discarded.** It is a third independent pass over 1831 and it agrees with the other two.

by: row 85, re-reading an act the archive had already read
what: Pasqua Falco was born on strada CAMELLARA, not strada COSTA — and the row's own evidence had said so for days
was: **PASQUA FALCO, born 30 March 1823**, stood in this archive with the place **«Arienzo, strada COSTA»** — the street her parents are on in their 1816 act.
now: **«Arienzo, strada CAMELLARA».** The act says «*è comparso **GIUSEPPE FALCO**, di anni **QUARANTADUE**, di professione **MASSARO DI CAMPAGNA**, domiciliato in questo Comune **strada CAMELLARA***».
how: The 1823 birth register was swept again at the **declarant band** for work-list row 85, and act 38 was opened a second time.
why:
**Nothing new was found; something already held was found to disagree with itself.** The street was carried forward from the household's 1816 act when the row was created and never corrected once the 1823 act was read — **although the quotation inside that same row says CAMELLARA twice**, and the row goes on to argue, at length, that *this is the very act on which strada Camellara stopped telling the two Giuseppe Falco apart*.

**The field and the evidence contradicted each other in one cell**, and the evidence was right. **A person page prints the field, not the paragraph** — so the site was publishing the wrong street for a woman whose street is the point.

It is recorded because a second band was run **expecting to find a new child and finding an old error instead**: re-reading an act this archive has already read is not wasted work.

by: row 85, on the first volume it touched
what: The second band found a Falco the first could not — ROSARIA FALCO, 15 March 1821, and a caution about how this archive tells two men apart
was: The Arienzo birth register for **1821** was swept on 21 September at the **parents band** and published here as holding **no Falco**. Work-list row **85** was then raised, saying that band can miss a **father** who declares his own child when the mother is not herself a Falco, and listing nine years owed a second pass.
now:
**The second pass found one in the first volume it touched.** Act 22: «*è comparso **GIUSEPPE FALCO, di anni TRENTOTTO**, di professione contadino, domiciliato in questo Comune, **strada CAMELLARA**, quale ci ha presentato una **FEMINA** … che la stessa è nata da **GELSOMINA VIGLIOTTA sua moglie legittima, di anni TRENTASETTE** … il nome di **ROSARIA***» — **15 March 1821**, at ten in the morning.

**The mother is a VIGLIOTTA.** The parents band reads her name and moves on; the Falco is the father, on the facing page. **That is the exact failure row 85 described, demonstrated within an hour of raising it.**
how: Sweeping the declarant band — `--band 0.34 0.19 --half R` — across the volume that had already been read the other way.
why:
**Two things follow, and the second is the more useful.**

**A second Rosaria.** The first died on **15 March 1819**; this one is born on **15 March 1821**, the same day of the same month, two years later. The coincidence is recorded and not explained. **Work-list row 42 is not answered** — it asks where the FIRST Rosaria's birth act is, and that is still nowhere — but the second Rosaria is now a documented person, and the naming habit that makes them two children is confirmed again.

**AND THE TEST THAT KEEPS THE TWO GIUSEPPE FALCO APART IS HALF WRONG.** This archive separates them «*by street and wife*»: one on **strada COSTA** with **Gelsomina Vigliotta**, one on **strada CAMELLARA** with **Antonia di Guida**. **Here the Gelsomina Vigliotta household is on strada Camellara.** The wife is the half that holds; **the street is not**. Nothing is merged — the 1816 and 1818 acts still name two different wives on one day's difference of stated age, which is the real evidence — but any reading resting on the street alone is unsafe, and at least one on this site did.

by: reading the 1832 and 1836 death registers against their own citations
what: An index said 3 December and the register says 3 SEPTEMBER — and the act's one word closes a join
was: **MARIANTONIA CIOFFI (the second)**, a child of Francesco Cioffi and Maria Falco, published as dying **3 December 1832**, cited to the **INDEX** — `an_ua14294`, *Morti indice 1832*, atto 64. **The register act had never been opened.**
now: **3 SEPTEMBER 1832**, and she is «**DI UN ANNO**». Act 64 of `an_ua14334`: «*… che nel giorno **TRE** del mese di **SETTEMBRE**, anno corrente, alle ore **NOVE**, è morta nella sua propria casa **MARIANTONIA CIOFFI, DI UN ANNO** … figlia di **FRANCESCO CIOFFI** … **e di MARIA FALCO***».
how: Opening the act the index points at — which nobody had done, because the index gave a name, a number and a date and looked like enough.
why:
**The age is what the index could not give, and it closes a join this archive flagged and would not claim.** On 21 September the birth act of an **ANTONIA** born **8 August 1831** to the same parents was found. «*Di un anno*» makes this her, dead at **one year and twenty-six days** — and it makes sense of the **second Antonia** the household names in 1831 after burying the first in 1823.

**An index row is not a record.** It gave the right act number and the wrong month, and it gave no age at all. This archive has now been caught by that three times in two days — a marriage index with the wrong day, a death index with the wrong month, and a death index that was the only source for a priest who turns out not to be in any register.

by: two death acts of 1836, read against three birth registers
what: Two Falco children were alive in 1835 and neither of their births is in any Arienzo register
was: **SALVATORE FALCO**, of Michele Falco and Mariantonia Vigliotta, and **PASQUALINA FALCO**, of Francescantonio Falco and Raffaela Falco, were held as two death dates in 1836 with nothing behind them.
now:
**Their ages, read from the acts, put both births in the middle of 1835 — and the registers do not have them.** Act 49, 9 August 1836: «*è morto … **SALVATORE FALCO, DI MESI QUATTORDICI***». Act 53, 14 September 1836: «*è morta … **PASQUALINA FALCO, DI MESI SEDICI***». Fourteen and sixteen months give **June 1835** and **May 1835**.

**The Arienzo birth registers for 1834, 1835 and 1836 have now been read at BOTH bands** — the parents band end to end and the declarant band end to end — **and there is no Falco in any of the three.**
how: Verifying two cited death acts, noticing that the ages pointed at a year this archive had just published as empty, and then going back and reading that year a second way rather than trusting the first pass.
why:
**One stray age is a clerk guessing. Two, from two households, pointing at the same six months, is something about the record.**

**And these parents registered their other children.** Maria Carmela (1832) and Raffaele (1837) are both in the register, both baptised the day they were born. **So the household's practice was to register, and two births are missing from it.**

What is left: the ages are wrong by more than a year in both acts; or both children were born outside Arienzo; or **the 1835 birth register is incomplete**. The third would matter well beyond this family, and it is the one this archive cannot yet test — the volume has **no tavola** to count against.

**A METHOD FAULT IS PUBLISHED WITH IT.** These volumes name the parents on the LEFT page of the next opening — but when the **father** is the declarant the left page says only «*da lui dichiarante*» and **his name is on the right page**. A parents-band sweep therefore catches Falco **mothers** and can miss Falco **fathers**. That gap is now closed for **1834, 1835 and 1836**; the nils already published for **1829, 1831, 1832, 1833, 1837 and 1838** rest on the parents band alone and are **owed a declarant-band pass**. Raised as its own row rather than quietly left.

what: A granddaughter of the founder, in an act that names him — ANGELA MARIA FALCO, 19 January 1822
was: **GIUSEPPE FALCO and ANTONIA DI GUIDA** — the founder's son and his wife — were documented with children running **Crescenzo, 11 October 1819**, then nothing until **Clemente, 11 March 1824**. A four-and-a-half-year gap, unexamined because the 1822 birth register had never been read.
now: **ANGELA MARIA FALCO, born 19 January 1822 at twelve, on strada Camellara.** Act 8: «*è comparso **GIUSEPPE FALCO FU MATTEO, di anni QUARANTA, di professione MASSARO**, domiciliato in questo Comune, **strada CAMELLARA**, quale ci ha presentato una **FEMINA** … che la stessa è nata da **ANTONIA DI GUIDA sua moglie legittima, di anni QUARANTA** … il nome di **ANGELA MARIA***». Witnessed by **OTTAVIO MIGLIORE**, thirty-nine, of strada Croce dell'Ospedale, and **GENNARO MAJONE SENIORE**, forty-three, *contadino*, of strada Caldarola. Baptised at **Sant'Andrea Apostolo the same day**.
how: Sweeping all 141 images of the 1822 birth register at the band that names both parents — looking for **Nunziata Falco**, who is not in it.
why:
**The act names Matteo.** «*Giuseppe Falco **FU MATTEO***» is the phrase this archive built a generation on: it is what separates the Camellara Giuseppe, this line's own, from the **Giuseppe Falco of strada Costa** who married Gelsomina Vigliotta, and it is why the infant Matteo of 1809 could be identified as the founder's grandson. **Here it is again, in a daughter's birth act, eight years after the notarial consent that first proved Matteo dead** — and it comes with his trade at that date, ***MASSARO***, a tenant farmer with stock rather than the *contadino* of his later acts.

**Both parents are given as forty**, which puts them about 1782. Antonia di Guida's baptism is **31 October 1783**. *Close enough for these registers, and not adopted.*

**And the sweep that found her was looking for someone else entirely.** Ten years of Arienzo birth registers have now been read act by act for a daughter of generation three who is in none of them. **The nils cost the same as the finds and are worth recording as carefully**; this one happened to pay.

what: A household kept a husband's surname this archive had already corrected — and a third act settles him
was: The household «**Domenico CRISCI & Margarita Falco**», created from one line of the 1819 Arienzo marriage index: «*ANGELO CRISCI ed ANNA RIVETTI | Arienzo | DI DOMENICO, e MARGARITA FALCO*». **This archive had already published that her husband was DOMENICO COSPI**, from her death act of 13 May 1836 — and the household kept the other name anyway.
now: **DOMENICO COSPI**, on a third document and in four separate places on one leaf. Arienzo *Nati* 1821, act 77: «*è comparso **DOMENICO COSPI, di anni CINQUANTASETTE**, di professione contadino, domiciliato in questo Comune, **strada COSPI***» — the margin of the leaf is annotated «**Cospi**», and the parish notice in the INDICAZIONE column names the baptised child «**ANNA MARIA TERESA COSPI**». **The household is renamed.**
how: Sweeping the 1821 birth register for a different child entirely — Nunziata Falco, who is not in it.
why:
**This is the fault this archive keeps finding in itself, in a new file.** A correction was made, published, and left to sit beside a household that went on carrying the retired name — the same shape as the surname conflations the corrections gate was written for, except that **the gate only checks `person` fields and this was in the household's NAME**.

**The son is deliberately left as CRISCI.** The 1819 index spells him *Angelo Crisci*, and that word has not been re-read at magnification. **Either the index misspells him as it misspelled his father, or he is not of this house** — and after a week in which *Cossi*, *Cioffi* and *Crisci* have each turned out to be the other at different magnifications, that is a reading job and not an inference.

**What the act gives beyond the name**: their first child, their street, and both their ages — he fifty-seven, she forty-one. Her death act of 1836 makes her sixty, implying 1776 against this act's 1780. **Four years apart, and neither adopted.**

## AND AN 1818 ACT COMPLICATES IT — 21 September 2026

Arienzo *Nati* **1818, act 9**, read from the image in **two hands** — the volume holds the year twice — gives «*è comparso **DOMENICO COSSI**, di anni QUARANTACINQUE, di professione contadino, domiciliato in detto comune, **strada COSSI** … e da **MARGARITA FALCO** sua moglie legittima, d'anni **QUARANTA***». **Three documents, three spellings: CRISCI in the 1819 index, COSSI in 1818, COSPI in 1821.**

**The household is NOT renamed again.** At this scan's resolution the same 1818 clerk's «**ANDREANA CRISCI**» — four leaves later, verified word for word in September and given as CRISCI in eight other acts — **is indistinguishable from a Cossi**: a flourished C, a narrow letter that will not resolve, a doubled long ſſ, a final i. **This hand's C-word is not a safe discriminator**, and the 1821 leaf, which says Cospi in four places including the parish notice, remains the strongest witness. *The variance is recorded; the name stands.*

by: row 31, twice over the same volume
what: A sweep that reads the DECLARANT does not read the father — and in these years the declarant is often the midwife
was: The Arienzo birth register for **1836** was swept at the **declarant** band — «*è comparso [name], di anni N, di professione X, domiciliato in strada Y*» — and reported here as **no Falco in 125 acts**. The band was chosen because in the first dozen acts the declarant was the child's father.
now: **That is not good enough, and the nil has been re-established on the right band before anything was built on it.** These acts begin on a **right** page and the **parents are named at the top of the NEXT LEFT page**. A declarant sweep silently drops every father whose child was carried to the Casa Comunale by the midwife.

**The failure mode is the dangerous one: it produces a clean, confident, complete-looking negative.** Every tile was legible, every act was accounted for, and the answer was wrong in a way nothing downstream could have caught.

**Both years are now read at the parents band** — 2–21% of the left page, three tiles wide at 2,400 pixels — and both hold no Vincenzo Falco. **The nil stands; the reasoning behind it did not.** Recorded rather than quietly redone, because the method is the thing other readers will copy.

what: Three Falco births in 1832 — and one household had never had a child at all
was: The Arienzo birth register for 1832 had never been read. **Aniello Crisci and Giovanna Falco** had stood since they were found on **one** record — their marriage of 6 September 1829 — with no children, no address and no second sighting.
now:
**PASQUALINA CRISCI, born 28 June 1832** at thirteen hours in **strada Crisci**, «*da **GIOVANNA FALCO, di anni VENTOTTO** … e da **ANIELLO CRISCI marito della stessa, di anni VENTISEI**, di professione contadino*», witnessed by **Angelo Migliore**, forty-three, *sartore*, and **Clemente Crisci**, twenty-eight, *calzolajo*. Giovanna Falco is a daughter of **Giuseppe Falco and Antonia di Guida**, so this is the founder's great-granddaughter.

**MARIA CARMELA FALCO, born 15 July 1832** at half past five in **strada Camellara**, to **Francescantonio Falco**, twenty-six, and **Maria Raffaela Falco**, eighteen.

**MARIA ROSA FALCO, born 20 July 1832** at eleven in **strada Camellara**, to **MICHELANGELO Falco**, twenty-six, and **Mariantonia Vigliotta**, twenty-eight.
how: Sweeping all 117 images of `an_ua14429` at the band that names both parents, looking for a different child entirely — Nunziata Falco, who is not there.
why:
**Two of the three raise questions rather than settling them, and both are left open.**

**Maria Carmela was born the day before her parents' wedding.** This archive dates the marriage of Francescantonio Falco and Raffaela Falco to **16 July 1832**, from the marriage index; she is born on the **15th**, and the act calls him «*marito della stessa*» — consistent, because a birth act is drawn a day or two after the birth. **Neither date is adjusted to fit the other**, and the index date is a church date that has never been read against a civil act.

**And Maria Rosa bears on a distinction this archive drew yesterday.** It files a Maria Rosa Falco's death of **30 May 1834** under «**Michele** Falco & Antonia Vigliotta» — the other of the two men proved distinct on 20 September, who both married an Antonia Vigliotti. Born 20 July 1832 she would be one year ten months at that death, which fits. **Either the household assignment is wrong, or there were two Maria Rosa Falco of two men whose names and whose wives' names both nearly coincide.** The birth act says MICHELANGELO, in full. **Nothing is moved on the strength of it**: the 1834 death act has not been re-read, and that is the test.

by: row 79, the last year with no index
what: Don Giuseppe Cioffi's death act does not exist in the Arienzo civil registers, and his reading is now marked as machine-derived
was: **DON GIUSEPPE CIOFFI**, fifty-six, *SACERDOTE*, son of Andrea Cioffi the *possidente* and Orsola Zimbardo, published as dying **4 December 1827** and cited to a leaf and an act that do not exist. The negative was then bounded year by year: 1826–1829 first, then the whole indexed run.

**The year buries eight religious and not one of them is he**: Don Gennaro Esposito, *sacerdote*, **ninety**; Don Alessandro Bruno, *sacerdote*, **twenty-seven**; Don Francesco de Gentij, *sacerdote*, **forty-six**; a Diglio *sacerdote*; Don Antonio Cimmino, ***seminarista***, **twenty-four**; Suor Fedele Ruggiero, **sixty-three**; Donna Carlotta Rauti, **seventy-three**; and **Donna Raffaela de' Falco**, *monaca*, **sixty-seven** — the gentry nun this archive already holds, her act confirmed here by accident.

It is not retired, and the difference matters.** Every element of it — the age, the trade, both parents — is independently confirmed by his sister **CELIA CIOFFI**'s act of 3 June 1843, which gives the same father, the same trade and the same mother. **The man is not in doubt; his own document is.** Retiring the reading would delete a person the archive can prove existed; leaving it unmarked would let a citation stand that points at nothing.

by: row 82, and the register's own order
what: The Falco of San Felice married in MARCH 1815, not May — and the correction published this morning carried the wrong month too
was: **LUIGI FALCO**, the soap-maker's son of San Felice a Cancello, was carried as marrying on «**19 [May] 1815**» — the month in brackets, this archive's mark for a reading it does not trust. **Hours earlier today the bracket was removed and «19 May 1815» published as fact**, in the entry that read his bride's name off the act for the first time.
now: **19 MARCH 1815.** The act reads «*a' dì **DICIANNOVE** del mese di **MARZO**, alle ore tredici*» — five letters ending in o, not the double-g descender pair of *Maggio*.
how:
**The register's own order proves it without the word.** Reading all fifteen acts of the first half in one pass gives an unbroken sequence: act 7 is **16 March**, act 8 is this one, act 9 is **21 March**, act 10 is **6 April**, and the volume runs in strict date order from 4 February to 2 December. **A 19 May here would sit between 16 March and 6 April**, which is impossible.

The same order was what proved the 1814 marriage act's month this morning, in a different volume. It is becoming this archive's cheapest test.
why:
**This is the second time today that removing a hedge published an error.** The bracket around «[May]» was there because nobody had read the month; reading the *bride* at last felt like reading the act, and the month went out unbracketed with everything else. **A correction is only as good as the words it actually looked at**, and the ones it did not look at inherit its new authority.

It also makes the sequence of that spring legible. **Seven marriages in thirty-four days** — 16, 19 and 21 March, then nothing until 6 April — and Luigi Falco, eighteen and a minor, brought his parents down from the Sei Casali to consent in person in the middle of it.

by: row 79, reading its own instructions against the coverage page
what: A work-list row told this archive to read six volumes that the coverage page already said were read
was: Work-list row 79, on the missing death act of **DON GIUSEPPE CIOFFI**, closed its last section with «***Still to try**: 1830–1835, and the parish burial register*».
now: **1830 to 1835 were already read, and so was every year from 1824 to 1843.** *What has been read* carries two rows saying so — the 1824–1830 sweep, and «*thirteen annual volumes, 55 images, every page's surname column cropped and tiled*» for 1831–1843.
how: Looking the row's instruction up on the page whose whole purpose is to answer that question, before opening a single image.
why:
**The negative is now far wider than the row believed, and better bounded.** He is absent from **twenty consecutive years** of Arienzo death indexes, with the **C** leaf opened in each. Only **1836** is unexamined, because that year has **no index in the series at all** — 1834's index is a single leaf, but it covers **A to C**, so it covers him.

**The fault is structural.** A work-list row's «still to try» is a *claim about what has not been done*, and **nothing in this archive checks it against the file that records what has been done.** This row would have sent a reader to open six volumes for nothing.

It is the same shape as the stale open question that asked what became of a daughter this archive had already buried: **a finding that lands in one file and never propagates to the file still asking the question** — except that here the two files are the **work list** and the **coverage register**, which are this archive's own instruments for not repeating itself.

by: row 82, reading the act behind an index row
what: The bride of the 1815 Falco marriage had three forenames in this archive, and two of them were wrong
was: Published from the 1815 marriage index alone: «*8. LUIGI FALCO | Arienzo | Di SEBASTIANO, e COLOMBA MONTEFUSCO*» ed «***GIUSTINA PETRILLO** | Arienzo | Fu SABATINO, e BRIGIDA COSSI*». The act itself had never been opened; the note behind it carried her as «*[?]ietta RENCHIELLO(?)*», with her mother «*[An]gela [?]*».
now: **The index says GIULIA. The act says STELLA.** «*è comparsa egualmente **STELLA PETRILLO** di anni diciotto, domiciliata in questa suddetta comune, **strada del Borgo**, di professione filatrice, **minore**, assistita da **BRIGIDA COSSI** sua madre di anni cinquantasei … essendo morto il padre **SABBATINO PETRILLO***.» **«Giustina» is neither**, and the mother is **Brigida**, not Angela.
how:
Rendering the act at 3,200 pixels and the index leaf at 3,000, and magnifying each disputed word to eight and fourteen times. The index forename carries a **G with a full descending loop** and reads *G-i-u-l-i-a*; the act's initial **does not descend below the line at all** and reads *S-t-e-l-l-a*.

**The surname went the other way, and it is the more useful lesson.** At survey width the act reads «**Vecchiello**» — that is what this reading was going to publish. At twelve times it is **PETRILLO**: eight letters, one dotted i, and **no second e before the double l**. The index agrees. *A word that changes when you magnify it was never read.*
why:
**Her parents are identical in both documents** — *fu Sabbatino Petrillo and Brigida Cossi* — so there is no doubt this is one woman, and the disagreement is confined to what she was called. **Both forenames are now recorded and neither is preferred**, because an act and an index are two clerks and this archive has no third document.

What cannot stand is the version that was published, which came from neither. It is the fourth time today that **a number or a name misread off an image became a fact nothing in the archive could challenge** — and the third time the challenge, when it came, came from opening the *other* document rather than from looking harder at the same one.

what: The test this archive uses to tell COSSI from CIOFFI does not work in every hand — and there is a better one
was: «*Cioffi has a **tall double-f ligature with a long descender**; Cossi a **short double-s with no ascender**.*» That is this archive's own three-way surname test, written from the 1825 register at full resolution, and it has decided several readings.
now:
**In the 1815 marriage register the doubled letters of COSSI descend exactly as a double f would.** So do the ones in **MASSONE** and in **SANSONE**, both of which are certainly a long ſ. **The descender does not separate them in that hand.**

**What does, in every hand: CIOFFI carries an i between the C and the o. COSSI does not.** *C-i-o-f-f-i* is six letters; *C-o-s-s-i* is five. At twelve times the difference is a dotted letter that is either there or not, and it does not depend on how the scribe finished his descenders.
how: Three instances in one volume, read at twelve times: **BRIGIDA COSSI** in act 8 and **ELISABETTA** and **MARINO COSSI** in act 21. All three show a C running straight into a round o with nothing between them, and all three have long descenders on the doubled letter.
why:
**The old test is not withdrawn — it is narrowed.** It was derived from one clerk's hand and it works there; it was being applied as though it were a property of the names. A test that depends on a scribe's habit will fail silently on the next scribe, and a surname decided by it will look settled.

**And it produced a real result in passing**: *Cossi* is a documented Arienzo surname, borne by two households in the 1815 marriages alone. The months this archive spent correcting *Cossi* to *Cioffi* on **strada Camellara** were about **one household**, not about the name — which is what the corrections said, and now there is a control that proves it.

what: «CAPODIUOMO» IS A STREET ARIENZO NEVER HAD — 219 rows corrected, after the first version of this entry was itself too big
was: **ANGELA FALCO**, the founder's daughter, was published as dying on **«strada CAPODIUOMO»** on 17 October 1822, and **GIOVANNI RIVETTI**, the *possidente* who declared his uncle's death in 1823, as living there too. The name stood in **nine places** across the household files, `line.json` and `plates.json`.
now:
**Six acts spanning the whole run were rendered at 3,200 pixels and magnified, and every one reads CAPODICONCA** — *C-a-p-o-d-i-c-o-n-c-a*, several of them twice in a single act:

| year | act | |
|---|---|---|
| **1817** | 11 | «domiciliato in questo comune, **strada Capodiconca**», twice |
| **1819** | 23 | «strada **Capodiconca**, e di Raffaele Giglio» |
| **1821** | 15 | «strada **Capodiconca**, vicino della defunta» — the one instance this archive's own note says was *checked at full resolution* |
| **1822** | 65 | three times in one act |
| **1823** | 51 | «strada **Capodiconca**, NIPOTE del defunto» |
| **1824** | 5 | twice, in a large clear hand that needs no magnification |

**And the corroboration from the other side**: the Arienzo BIRTH registers for **1832 and 1836**, read out act by act on 21 September, give **strada Capodiconca** constantly and **strada Capodiuomo not once**.

**219 rows are corrected** — in `data/sweep-people.tsv`, the published register and nine years of death-register notes. **Eleven are deliberately left alone**: the five 1837 and four 1838 sweep rows and their register entries. **The 1837 hand is too rapid to decide at this scan's limit** and a word this archive cannot read is not a word it may change.
how: Counting first, then reading. The first version of this entry generalised from two acts; the count — **228 Capodiuomo against 707 Capodiconca in the same files** — took one command and had not been run. Six acts were then chosen to span the run, **both ends and the middle**, and rendered at full resolution.
why:
**The misreading is this archive's, not the clerks'.** It is confined to the **1817–1825 death-register sweeps** — a single continuous stretch of one kind of work — and it stops dead after 1825 apart from nine stragglers in 1837–1838. **That distribution is the fingerprint of a reading habit, not of a street that existed for eight years.**

**What it had already produced.** Angela Falco, the founder's daughter, was published as having «*moved from strada Camellara to strada Capodiuomo*» — a fact about a widow's last years resting entirely on the word. And the 1823 act was read as tying «*the propertied Rivetti of Capodiuomo*» to this family through a nephew. **Both statements survive with the right street name**; neither would have been findable by anyone searching the real one.

**This entry was corrected twice before it was right**, and both versions are above. The first said the street did not exist, from two acts. The second withdrew that as an overclaim and opened a row. **The third counted, read six acts, and closed it.** The middle step was not wasted — it is what stopped 228 rows being changed on the strength of two readings.

what: Two citations off by one — an image number, and a digit in a marriage index
was: **«ANTENATI an_ua14335 img9L act16»** for the death of **Pasquale Falco, aged three**, son of Vincenzo Falco and Andreana Crisci, on 22 February 1833. And **«the church date given as 24 MARZO»** for **Angelandrea Falco's** marriage of 1847, taken from that year's marriage index.
now: **The act is on image 10, not image 9**, and **the index says 29 MARZO, not 24.**
how:
Image 9 left of the 1833 death register is **act 14, of 19 February**, and the dead there is a woman. **Even acts run down the left page of each opening in these registers and odd acts down the right** — the same structure that proved the 1814 marriage act this morning — so act 16 is on image **10 left**, and there it is: «*è morto nella sua propria casa **PASQUALE FALCO, di anni TRE**, … figlio di **VINCENZO FALCO** … e di **ANDREANA CRISCI***», at one at night on 22 February, declared by two neighbours of strada Camellara.

The index digit carries a **full descender loop**; the act number **4** two rows above it on the same page has none.
why:
**The index date could have been challenged without opening anything.** Under the Restoration system the civil *solenne promessa* comes first and the church celebration follows, so a church date of 24 March against a promise of 29 March is **impossible on its face**. The act's own INDICAZIONE column, which copies the parish priest's certificate, spells the day out: «*è seguita nel giorno **VENTINOVE** del mese di Marzo*». Act 20 of 1848 shows the usual shape — promise 19 August, church 23 August.

**Everything else in the last five volumes held.** Act 3 of 1847, act 20 of 1848, act 65 of 1822 and act 9 of 1829 verify word for word, including the two Domenico Crisci who declared Luca Crisci's death — one «**PARENTE DEL DEFUNTO**», one «**VICINO**», on the same street, an hour apart in the same act.

by: row 58, re-reading a volume it had already passed as clean
what: The bride of 1850 was THIRTY-NINE, not nineteen — and the act said so in the word beside the number
was: Published here and in the household file on 20 September 2026, from the Arienzo marriage register of 1850, act 6: «*… e **GIOVANNA D'AMBROGIO maggiore, di anni DICIANNOVE**, di professione contadina*». The volume was reported in the work list as **clean**, with the words «*every word holds*».
now: **«di anni TRENOVE»** — the clerk's contraction of *trentanove*, **thirty-nine**. She was born about **1811**, not about 1831, and she was eight years younger than the widower she married rather than twenty-four.
how: Re-rendering the leaf at its full **3,200 pixels** instead of the 1,700 the first pass used. At that size the numeral's initial is a **tall ascender crossed by a diagonal — a t**. This hand's **d** is a small closed bowl with a short back-leaning ascender, and there is one four lines above in the same pen, in «**CHIARA RIVETTI DEFUNTA**». The two letters are not alike at full resolution and are hard to tell apart below it.
why:
**The contradiction was on the page in words, not in handwriting, and nobody read it.** The same sentence calls her «**MAGGIORE**» — of age — and then «nineteen». Under the code in force a woman under twenty-one was «**MINORE**» and could not marry without a parent's consent: this archive publishes exactly that, four lines of a different act, where **Andreana Crisci in 1814 is «figlia minore assistita da Arcangelo Crisci suo padre»**. Giovanna's father was dead, her mother is named, and **no consent is taken**. 

So the reading could have been challenged without opening the image at all — and the note that carried it said «*every word holds*». **A volume reported clean is the least likely thing in this archive to be re-read**, which is the second time in one day that a verification pass has had to correct itself rather than a source.

what: There is no act 26. Generation three married on 15 OCTOBER 1814, and one line of one image was misread three ways
was: Published since September 2026, on the front page, on /antenati, on /processetti, on /camellara, on /families and in five data files: «*His civil marriage act — Arienzo, **act 26 of 15 December 1814** — records him as **aged 21**, a contadino, and “figlio maggiore di Pasquale Falco”*». An earlier session transcribed it from the image and cited the ark and the page.
now: **«NUMERO D'ORDINE 16. L'anno mille ottocento [tredici struck, QUATTORDICI written above] a' dì QUINDICI 15 del mese di OTTOBRE, ad ore ventitre … è comparso VINCENZO FALCO di anni VENTITRE, di professione CONTADINO, domiciliato in questo Comune, strada CAMELLARA, figlio maggiore di PASQUALE FALCO di anni cinquanta … qui presente e dando il suo consenso.»** Three elements of that one line were wrong: **the act number (16, not 26), the month (October, not December) and the groom's age (twenty-three, not twenty-one)**. The day — «quindici 15», written in words and figures — was right, which is why it survived every re-reading.
how:
**The register's own order proves the month without reading a letter of it.** The 1814 marriage register runs its even acts down the left page of each opening and its odd acts down the right. Act 14 is **2 October**, act 15 is **6 October**, act 17 is **2 December** — and act 17 sits on the page facing act 16. Act 16 therefore falls between 6 October and 2 December, and **15 December is after act 17 and impossible**. The volume then runs out: folio 29 is a blank pre-printed form and folio 30 closes the book. **There is no act 26 in it.**

The reading itself was then confirmed letter by letter at the scan's full resolution, and it agrees with the **1814 marriage index**, read independently five days earlier, which gives «*16. VINCENZO FALCO … A 15 OTTOBRE 1814*».
why:
**The archive had both answers in it at once and neither file could see the other.** `households.json` carried 15 October from the index; `line.json`, `plates.json` and `processetti.json` carried 15 December from this transcription. Nothing compares them, so a contradiction on **the wedding day of the couple this whole line descends through** sat in the published site for five days.

**And the wrong number did damage.** A whole search was mounted for «act 26's supporting file», reported on *Searched* as **blocked** — «*the 1814 volume runs to act 25 and stops; act 26's file is in neither volume*» — and written into the research queue as a dead end. The file was never missing. It is **bundle 16**, which is the number it always should have been.

The digit that went wrong is the **first** one, and it went wrong the same way three times in this family's paperwork: **16 read as 26**, **86 read as 26**, and — on a heading struck here on 15 September — **1814 read as 1812**. In each case the true digit became a 2.
by: reading an_ua14218 image 9 at the scan's limit, and the four acts around it

what: The parents consented in SEPTEMBER, not December — and Pasquale Falco signed his own name
was: «*a notarial act of **8 December 1814** before Felice Morgillo in which “li conjugi PASQUALE FALCO del fu MATTEO, e CHIARA RIVETTI del fu NICOLA” consent*» — on the front page, on /rivetti, on /crisci, on /processetti and in `line.json`, where it also fixed the bracket on Matteo Falco's death at «*[1786, **8 Dec 1814**]*».
now: **8 SEPTEMBER 1814.** The act is headed «*Il giorno **OTTO 8** del Mese di **SETTEMBRE** dell'Anno Milleottocento, e quattordici 1814*», and the registration endorsement at its foot reads «*Reg[istra]to in Arienzo li **DODICI SETTEMBRE 1814**.*» The bride's parents consented the same day, before the same notary, in **act 86** — not «act 26», and not before a «Salvio» Morgillo, who never existed: both acts open «*Son comparsi avanti di me **FELICE MORGILLO del fu Valeriano***».
how:
Magnifying the month. The initial is a long ſ with a descender and **no closed bowl** — the same letter that opens «*Son comparsi*» three lines below it on the same page, and «*sedici*» and «*settembre*» in the banns. A *Dicembre* would begin with a capital D. The endorsement at the foot of the facing page then gives the month again, in a different hand, spelled out.

**The sequence only closes once the December is gone.** Consent on 8 September, registered 12 September, banns on Sunday 11 and Sunday 18 September, marriage on 15 October. With a December consent the parents were signing five weeks *after* the banns and ten weeks after — or, on the old reading, two months *before* — a wedding that had already happened.
why:
**And there is something in this act that no other document in the archive holds.** The notary closes act 85: «*quindi si è firmato soltanto il detto **PASQUALE FALCO**, avendo la detta **CHIARA RIVETTI** dichiarato di **NON SAPERE SCRIVERE***» — and below it, in a large, slow, unjoined hand quite unlike his own, stands **«PASCALE FALCO»**. He spells it *Pascale*.

It is **the only autograph of anyone in this line**: seven generations of contadini and braccianti, and one man's name in his own hand, on a September afternoon in a notary's house on strada Terra Murata, consenting to his eldest son's marriage. His wife could not write. Twenty years later he was buried from strada Camellara.

what: WITHDRAWN — processetti bundles are NOT numbered in a sequence of their own. The rule was invented to reconcile a discrepancy that did not exist
was: Published 13 September 2026 and repeated on /processetti and /method ever since: «*processetti **BUNDLES** are numbered in their own sequence, **in the order the banns were published** — not by the number the marriage later received in the marriage register. The 1814 volume holds SEVENTEEN bundles; Vincenzo and Adriana published in September and married in December, so their file is **bundle 16** while their marriage is **act 26***.»
now: **Their marriage is act 16.** The bundle number and the act number are the same number. The volume's own second example settles it: the archive identified **bundle 17** as *Francesco Crisci fu Alessandro × Teresa Morgillo*, published 20 November 1814 — and the marriage register's **act 17**, read on 20 September 2026, is *Francesco Crisci and Teresa Morgillo*, 2 December 1814, on the page facing act 16.
how: Reading the 1814 marriage register end to end, eleven images, and matching every act number to the bundle covers this archive had already read.
why:
**This is the same failure as the volume that was said to hold three years, struck here on 15 September — a general rule built on top of a misreading, and published as a method.** The rule was not idly wrong: it told the next reader that bundle *N* has nothing to do with act *N*, which is the opposite of the truth, and it would have sent them past the right bundle.

**The practical advice survives, for a better reason than the one first given.** Match a processetti bundle on the **names and the publication date**, not on the act number — not because the numbers differ, but because nothing in the volume promises they agree, while a match on names cannot be wrong.

What it cost is worth naming. The wrong act number produced a wrong negative («act 26's file is not in the volume»), the wrong negative produced a queue entry telling everyone not to look, and when the file was found anyway the discrepancy produced **a false rule** — which then had to be corrected once for a wrong illustration before being withdrawn entirely. **Four errors, all of them descended from a 1 read as a 2.**

what: identification
was: AGOSTINO FALCONE at the head of the line
now: MATTEO FALCO — and Falcone discarded

what: a dead end that was not one
was: “The file for marriage act 26 (Falco × Crisci) is not in the 1814 processetti. Do not search these two again.”
now: It was there — bundle 16, images 265–274 — and it is the richest document this archive has found.
how: An earlier session worked the volume from the back, found a publication act numbered 25 dated 20 November 1814 and then the 1815 divider, and concluded the volume stopped short of act 26. But processetti BUNDLES are numbered in their own sequence, in the order the banns were published — not by the number the marriage later received in the marriage register. The 1814 volume holds SEVENTEEN bundles; Vincenzo and Adriana published in September and married in December, so their file is bundle 16 while their marriage is act 26. The «25» that stopped the earlier search was a publication act number inside bundle 17, the last of the year.
why: This is the most expensive kind of error an archive can make — a wrong negative, written down as a rule, that stops anyone looking again. It stayed in QUEUE.md under “Dead ends, recorded so they are not repeated” for weeks. The standing rule is now: in a processetti volume match on names and publication date, never on the marriage act number — and every “do not search again” note must carry the reasoning that produced it, so the reasoning can be checked.

what: a birth date
was: Vincenzo Falco, generation three, born 1793
now: Baptised 1 February 1792 — and christened Vincenzo RAFFAELE
