**The act says April, and it names her mother.** «*…i quali hanno dichiarato che a' detto dì **NOVE** del mese corrente di **APRILE** ad ore dodici, **GAETANA LAUDATO** figlia delli furono **GIACINTO LAUDATO** e **VITTORIA RUOTOLO**, vedova di **SIMONE MORGILLO***».

**The month was wrong by one, and «Giovanna —» — a forename with the surname marked unread — is in fact VITTORIA RUOTOLO, written plainly.** The declarants are her own sons, **ANGELO MORGILLO, 48**, and **GIUSEPPE MORGILLO, 71**, entered as «*figli della defunta*».
how: Work-list row 58 — verifying that the archive's ANTENATI citations resolve to the acts they name. `an_ua14318` was the second volume checked.
why:
**A wrong month is the kind of error that never announces itself.** Nothing downstream contradicted it, and it would have been copied forward every time the Morgillo pedigree was rebuilt.

**The mother is the larger gain.** «Giovanna —» told the next reader the surname was lost to the page. It was not lost; it was never read. **VITTORIA RUOTOLO is a grandmother this archive can now look for**, and the Ruotolo are already in these registers.

**And the same volume produced the other kind of error.** Donna Francesca Rivetti's death was cited at **img7L**; image 7 left carries atto 10, somebody else entirely. **The act is on img8L**, and says exactly what this archive said it says. **The fact was right and the leaf reference was wrong** — which is the failure this row exists to catch, and which no reader could have found without opening the leaf.

**Of 35 citations checked in two volumes, 33 resolve exactly.** The 1817 volume — 22 citations, including the act that settles generation four — is clean.

what: Two more dates off by a single day — and the shape of every citation error so far
was: **SUOR MARIA MADDALENA RIVETTI**, the nun whose act is one of three signs of a Rivetti house of standing at Arienzo, was published as dying **30 March 1819**. **CARLANTONIO MORGILLO** was published as declaring a death on **20 October 1819** — his fifth sighting, and part of the age series this archive uses to show these registers guess.
now: **Both are one day out.** The nun's act reads «*L'anno mille ottocento diciannove a' dì **TRENTUNO** del mese di Marzo*», and repeats it: «*a' detto dì trentuno … ad ore ventidue*». **31 March.** Carlantonio Morgillo's reads «*a' dì **VENTUNO** del mese di Ottobre*». **21 October.** Both words were magnified before either record was touched; the «-uno» is unambiguous in each.
how: Work-list row 58 — verifying that this archive's ANTENATI citations resolve to the acts they name. Four volumes are now checked: **59 citations, five errors.**
why:
**The pattern matters more than the two days.** Of the five errors found in fifty-nine citations, **not one is a misread name, a wrong parent, or an invented relationship.** Every single one is **a date word or a leaf number** — «trenta» read for «trentuno», «venti» for «ventuno», «marzo» for «aprile», and an act cited at img7L that is on img8L.

**This archive reads its people well and its numbers carelessly.** That is a useful thing to know about oneself, because a wrong name gets caught — somebody downstream notices a person who cannot exist — and **a wrong day never does.**

**The same pass confirmed the archive's most-quoted detail to the hour.** **DOMENICO FALCO** died «*ad ore dodici*» on 15 March 1819 and **ROSARIA FALCO** «*ad ore ventitré*» the same day: **eleven hours apart**, exactly as published, in two acts drawn on consecutive days by the same clerk.

what: Luigi Falco's birth was cited as act 133 — it is act 134, and act 133 is a family that looks just like his
was: **LUIGI FALCO**, son of Vincenzo Falco and Andreana Crisci, born **21 December 1819** — cited here as **`an_ua14416` img71L act 133**. His birth date is load-bearing: his death act of 16 December 1864 is used to show the register's stated age is wrong by three, «*born 21 December 1819, he died five days short of forty-five and the act says forty-one*».
now:
**The leaf is right and the number is not.** Image 71 left is headed «*Numero d'ordine **CENTOTRENTAQUATTRO***». **The act is 134.**

**And act 133 — on the facing leaf, image 70 right — is a different family that could pass for this one:** «*L'anno mille ottocento diciannove a' dì **ventuno** del mese di **Dicembre** … è comparso **VINCENZO MAURO**, di anni ventisette, di professione **viaticale**, domiciliato in questo comune **strada Sant'Andrea** … è nata … da **ANDREANA CARFORA** sua moglie legittima, d'anni ventisei, un **Maschio** che ci ha presentato*».

**Same day. Same clerk. A Vincenzo and an Andreana in each, both presenting a boy.** Only the surnames differ — Mauro and Carfora against Falco and Crisci — and the street.
how: Work-list row 58, the fifth volume checked. The act numbers on both leaves were magnified before anything was changed.
why:
**This is the most dangerous kind of citation error this archive has found.** A wrong leaf sends you to a blank page and you notice. **A wrong act number sends you to the act next door**, and here the act next door is a couple with the same two forenames, on the same day, in the same hand. **Nothing but the surname would have stopped a reader adopting it**, and the date and the sex both agree.

**Everything else in the volume verified, including the act this archive's whole margin method was built on.** Domenico Clemente Falco's birth of 18 March 1819 carries, below the act, «*Con atto **6 Agosto 1856** atto **21** in **S. Maria a Vico** il Falco sposò **DOMENICA VIGLIOTTI***» — a marriage in another comune, written in the margin of a birth, exactly as published.

**One date is flagged and deliberately left alone.** Act 22 is cited at 19 February 1819 and the word looks like «diciotto». **At the leaf's full resolution it cannot be separated from «diciannove».** It stays as published. **A date this archive cannot read is not a date it may change.**

what: Giuseppe Falco was forty-two in June 1823, not forty-three
was: «*e **GIUSEPPE FALCO FU MATTEO**, di anni **quarantatre**, di professione Contadino, regnicolo, domiciliato strada Camellara*» — Arienzo Morti 1823, `an_ua14325` img20R. The act matters out of all proportion to its size: **it is the first civil record to state his parentage outright**, and the archive reasoned from the age that he was born about 1780.
now: The word ends **«-adue»**. It is **«quarantadue»** — forty-two — so born about **1781**.
how: Work-list row 58. The tail of the word was magnified against the same clerk's «tre», written three lines below on the same leaf in «Maria Crisci, di anni tre». The two shapes do not match: «tre» is three strokes, open and wide, and the age word has a «d» loop, a two-arched «u» and a compressed «e».
why: **The conclusion survives and the number does not.** Forty-two in June 1823 gives about 1781; the thirty-seven he gives in October 1817 gives about 1780. The two still agree within a year, which is inside the noise this archive has already demonstrated — the same registers make one man forty on 2 April 1825 and forty-five four days later. **What changes is the archive's right to quote the word.** It was quoting a word it had not read.

what: Three dates in the 1843 death register were wrong, and one of them by two months
was: From Arienzo Morti 1843, `an_ua14345`: **Antonio Cioffi**, seventeen days old, son of Raffaele Cioffi and Francesca Falco, published at **10 June 1843** (act 17). **Aniello Cioffi**, seventy-six, son of Gioacchino Cioffi and the elder Francesca Falco, published at **27 July 1843** (act 29). **Gennaro Morgillo**, fifty-three, colono, published at **14 August 1843** (act 33).
how: Work-list row 58, the seventh volume checked. Act 17 is written «*del mese di **Aprile***» on both of its date lines, and the month word was magnified twice. Act 29 is drawn on the twenty-seventh but declares the death «*nel giorno **ventisei***» — the archive had recorded the day the clerk wrote, not the day the man died. Act 33 reads «*il dì **quattro** del mese di Agosto*», and **the acts on either side of it settle it arithmetically**: act 32 is 3 August and act 35 is 10 August, so act 33 cannot be the fourteenth.
why:
**Three errors in one volume, and all three are the same kind of error this row keeps finding.** Across seven volumes and ninety-five citations there are now ten mistakes, and **not one of them is a misread name, a wrong parent or an invented relationship**. Every one is a number — a date word, an age, a leaf, an act. **The archive reads its people well and its numbers carelessly**, and a number is exactly what no reader downstream can check without going back to the film.

Antonio Cioffi's two months matter most: seventeen days old on 10 April means **born about 24 March 1843**, not late May.

what: The archive said a Falco-Morgillo marriage was thirty years away while holding the act that made it eighteen months
was: Of Gennaro Morgillo's death act of 1843: «*It is the closest the record comes to the **Falco-Morgillo marriage that was still thirty years away***.» The act records **GENNARO MORGILLO**, fifty-three, **colono** of **strada Camellara**, **widower of a Felicia**, son of **Angelo Morgillo** defunto, colono of the Monticello de' Cappuccini — and his death was declared by **GIUSEPPE FALCO**, colono of that same street.
now:
**The marriage was eighteen months away, and this archive already held it.** On **2 February 1845** **CRESCENZO FALCO**, Giuseppe's son, married **ANGELA MARIA MORGILLO**, twenty-three, of **strada Cappuccini**: «*figlia di **GENNARO MORGILLO DEFUNTO**, di professione **colono**, e di **MARIA FELICIA SANSONE** … **defunta***».

The two men are now published as **PROBABLY the same man** — forename, surname, trade, the wife's forename, the order in which the couple died, and the street that climbs to his father's hill all agree — and **the identification is graded and not asserted**, because Morgillo is the commonest surname in these registers and this archive already holds two distinct Angelo Morgillo.
how: Work-list row 58. Verifying the act's DATE meant reading the act, and reading the act meant reading the name in it.
why:
**Nothing was missing. Two files were.** The death act sat in one household and the marriage in another, and the sentence that judged the death act had been written without looking at the marriage. **At this size the likeliest wrong statement in the archive is one of its own, left standing where a finding never travelled** — and this one was wrong by twenty-eight years.

**What it is not, yet, is proven.** The *processetto* for the 1845 marriage must carry Gennaro Morgillo's death certificate with its act number on it. If the number is 33 of 1843, the question closes; that is now work-list row 73.

what: «PIVERA» was corrected on 14 September and the person pages went on publishing it for six days
was: **ANTONIA DI GUIDA's mother** was published on her person page and in her household as «*filiam Josephi e **Magdalenae PIVERA***», and again under her husband as «*dau of Giuseppe & Maddalena **Pivera***».
now: «*filiam Josephi, et **Magdalenae RIVETTA***», and «*dau of **GIUSEPPE DI GUIDA** & **MADDALENA RIVETTA***».
how: Not by reading anything new. **The archive had already read it** — from the image, on 14 September 2026, against a control on the next line of the same act in the same pen, «*servata forma Ritu: Roma:*», whose two capital **R** match the initial exactly. **The corrected reading was written into `data/households.tsv` and never into `site/src/data/households.json`**, and the site is built from the second. Found on 20 September while mirroring an unrelated edit between the two files.
why:
**PIVERA was never a reading. It was an OCR guess**, copied into this archive without being checked, and the household it belongs to has been called **«Giuseppe di Guida & Michedalena Rivetti»** on this site the whole time — so the archive was contradicting itself on one page.

**The fault is not the letter. It is that a correction stopped halfway.** This archive keeps the same facts in a TSV and a JSON, edits both by hand, and has a gate that checks they agree on *who is in which household* — not on *what the evidence says*. **Thirty-seven rows disagree**; most are harmless drift where one file holds a fuller note, but three carried readings the published site had never seen. All three are now adopted, and **work-list row 75 exists to close the gap properly and to make the gate check the evidence too.**

what: The child Giuseppe Falco buried in 1826 was a CIOFFI, and his father was CESARE, not Gaspare Cossi
was: Of Giuseppe Falco's appearance as a declarant on 9 August 1826: «*declaring atto 56, the death of **Giuseppe COSSI**, two, son of **GASPARE COSSI** and Maria Sposito*». Arienzo Morti 1826, `an_ua14328` img32L.
now: «*è morto nella sua propria casa **GIUSEPPE CIOFFI**, d'anni due … figlio di **CESARE CIOFFI**, di professione contadino, domiciliato ivi, e di **MARIA SPOSITO**, domiciliata ivi*».
how: Work-list row 58, the eighth volume. Both names magnified. The surname carries the **double-f ligature with its long descender** that this archive has already had to learn once; the father's forename is **Cesare**, written with the long ſ, which is what was being read as a «p» in «Gaspare».
why:
**Two misread NAMES — the first this row has found.** Seven volumes and ninety-five citations had produced nothing but wrong numbers, and the archive had begun to say so as if it were a law. **It is not a law. It is a tendency, and this volume broke it.**

**The act also states a kinship the archive was not holding.** Its first declarant is «*SALVATORE SPOSITO, di anni ventisei, contadino … strada Camellara, **ZIO DEL DEFUNTO***» — the dead child's uncle, and so the mother's brother. **The 1826 reading log had recorded that «zio» when the volume was read. It never reached a household**, which is the third time this archive has found a fact harvested and not held.

**One thing that has NOT been done, deliberately.** «Cossi» stands 43 times in this archive's register, nearly all of it harvested from other people's indexes. **One act has now been read at full resolution and it said Cioffi twice.** That is one act, not a rule. Both surnames exist in Arienzo. **Nothing has been renamed in bulk, and nothing should be until the acts are read.**

what: Angelo Sansone was forty-six at Maria Falco's death, not forty-five — and his surname settled another act
was: «*Declared by **ANGELO SANSONE, 45**, and Tomaso Sposito, 50, both contadini of strada Camellara, each as «vicino», not «parente»*» — at the death of **MARIA FALCO**, wife of Alfonso Diglio, daughter of Pasquale Falco and Chiara Rivetti, 25 April 1826.
now: «*di anni **quarantasei***» — **forty-six**. Tomaso Sposito's fifty is right, and so is everything else in the act.
how: Work-list row 58. Arienzo Morti 1826, `an_ua14328` img13L act 22.
why:
**The age is trivial. What his surname did is not.** Magnifying «*Angelo **Sanſone***» in this act gave the archive a control it had been missing two volumes earlier: **the same long ſ, in the same shape, in the same street**. It is what settled the surname of **FELICIA SANSONE**, wife of the Gennaro Morgillo who died in 1843 — published here as «Sompone», where the «p» was a long s all along — and so it is what turned a four-way agreement into a five-way one for the identification of **Crescenzo Falco's father-in-law**.

**A control letter is worth more than a confident reading**, and this archive keeps relearning it.

what: A commit message that quoted a noindex tag became one, and de-indexed the page it was printed on
was:
**`/changes` is generated from this archive's own commit history**, and the kit renders each entry's summary as HTML. One of those commits is «*Living people noindexed, Lucia Coppa never existed…*», and its summary **quotes the very tag it had just added** — a `robots` meta element carrying *noindex, nofollow*, written out in full, angle brackets and all.

**Astro wrote that straight into the page.** `/changes` de-indexed itself, the build's own sitemap listed it anyway, and **the deploy failed twice before it was found**.
now: `tools/build_changes.py` now escapes the subject and the summary — **angle brackets and quotes both** — before writing them. **A commit message is data, not markup.**
how: David reported the failed deploy. The job log named the page.
why:
**The entry had been in the file for nine days and had never rendered, because `changes.json` was stale** — the same fault found the same morning in `researchlog.json`. Regenerating it from git, correctly, is what made the tag real. **A generator that has not been run is not a generator; it is a cache nobody is checking.**

**Escaping only the angle brackets was not enough**, and the second attempt failed too: what the gate greps for is the *text* of the attributes, not the brackets, so the quotation marks had to be escaped as well.

**And then this very correction brought the build down a third time.** Written out plainly, it quoted the tag once more — and `/corrections` renders its own prose as HTML too. **The sentence describing the bug reproduced it.** It is now written in words instead, and that is the standing rule for these pages: **describe markup, never quote it.**

**The two guards also disagree with each other.** The sitemap builder looks for a noindex tag **in the first 4,000 bytes** of a page; the archive checker reads the whole file. A noindex deep in a page's body is therefore invisible to one and fatal to the other. **That is in the shared kit, which another session owns, and it is reported rather than patched here** — work-list row 76.

what: Marta Cioffi was seven years old, and the words this archive put in quotation marks are not in the act
was: «*È morta nella sua propria casa **MARTA CIOFFI D'UN MESE**.*» **One month old** — published with the Italian in quotation marks, in the household file and in the 1840 reading log. Arienzo Morti 1840, act 73, `an_ua14342` img45R.
now: «*è morta nella sua propria casa **MARTA CIOFFI d'anni SETTE***» — **seven years old**, born about 1833. Died at eight in the morning on **6 November 1840**.
how: Work-list row 58, the tenth volume. The words were magnified before anything was changed; «d'anni sette» is written plainly and is not close to «d'un mese».
why:
**This is the worst error this row has found, and it is not the number.** A wrong age is a wrong number and a reader can suspect it. **A quotation the document does not contain cannot be suspected at all** — it is the one thing on this site that is supposed to be beyond argument. **The archive invented a sentence and set it in quotation marks.**

**The same act mis-aged both its declarants**: CLEMENTE CIOFFI is thirty-six, not thirty-four, and VIRGILIO CIOFFI is twenty-three, not twenty-eight.

**Nothing about the family changes.** Marta is still the daughter of Giovanni Cioffi and Maria Porrino of strada Camellara. **What changes is that she lived seven years and this archive had buried her at one month.**

what: «The steadiest age series in these registers» was wrong at both ends, and the man got younger
was: Of **GIOVANNI CIOFFI**, the contadino of strada Camellara who reported Chiara Rivetti's death: «*his stated age is, after the first entry, the steadiest series in these registers: **FORTY in 1840, FORTY-SEVEN in August 1842, FORTY-EIGHT in September 1843**. In a register that gives Giuseppe Falco eleven different ages, **this clerk got one right**.*» A second page said the same thing in fewer words.
now:
**The 1840 act gives him no age at all.** He appears in it as the dead child's father, and fathers are not aged in these acts. **The 1843 act says FORTY-THREE, not forty-eight.**

The series is: **forty-seven in August 1842, forty-three in September 1843.** He got four years younger in thirteen months.
how: Work-list row 58. «*di anni quarantasette*» and «*di anni quarantatre*» were magnified side by side; they are visibly different words, the second two letters shorter.
why:
**The archive had already read the 1843 act correctly.** On 15 September 2026 it magnified that act, published thirty-three and forty-three for the two declarants, and corrected Chiara Rivetti's page — **and left «forty-eight» standing in two other files, still carrying the conclusion built on it.** That is the same fault as «Pivera», found the same morning: a correction that reached one file.

**The inversion is what matters.** The one man this archive held up as proof that a clerk could keep an age straight turns out to be another proof that they could not — which is what the rest of the evidence here has said all along.

what: Donna Serafina Cimmino never existed, and neither did the discrepancy built on her
was: A household named «**Stefano Scarpati & [Serafina/Faustina] Cimmino**», holding a person called **DONNA SERAFINA CIMMINO**, and this note: «*THE ONE DISCREPANCY, AND IT IS PUBLISHED RATHER THAN RESOLVED. The 1840 act names the mother **SERAFINA** Cimmino; the 1842 act names her **FAUSTINA** Cimmino… Either a clerk misread a forename, or Stefano Scarpati married twice.*»
now: **Both acts say FAUSTINA.** The 1840 act reads «*e di **Donna FAUSTINA CIMMINO Defunta**, domiciliata ivi*» — the capital **F** with its crossbar, and the «au» after it. The household is now **Stefano Scarpati & Faustina Cimmino**.
how: Work-list row 58. Arienzo Morti 1840 act 28, `an_ua14342` img17L, read at the leaf's full resolution.
why:
**The misreading was this archive's, and it manufactured two things out of nothing**: a woman with a name and a page, and a genealogical problem — a possible second marriage — that was then published as an open discrepancy, honestly flagged, and entirely imaginary. **Publishing a doubt is only honest when the doubt is real.**

**It buys something back.** The archpriest of Arienzo, **DON ANGELO SCARPATI**, and the sorora of the Conservatorio di San Filippo, **MARIA GIUSEPPA SCARPATI**, are now named in two acts two years apart with **the same father, the same rank, the same trade and the same mother**. It remains an inference — two death acts are not a birth record — but the objection against it is gone.

what: The man who declared beside Giuseppe Falco's street in 1842 was not a Cioffi
was: «**ANTONIO CIOFFI**, thirty-two, a contadino of strada Camellara — a further Cioffi on the Falco street» — the first declarant at the death of the two-year-old Matteo Falco, Arienzo Morti 1842 act 55, `an_ua14344` img35R.
now:
**He is not a Cioffi.** The control is two lines below him in the same act — **GIOVANNI CIOFFI**, written with the unmistakable double-f ligature and its long descender. **This word has no such ligature.** It reads **«Gasparo»**, and **Gasparo is an Arienzo surname**: the 1834 death register has **Elena Lettieri, «widow of ANGELO GASPARO»**, and the same volume records a **strada Gasparro**.

**The reading «Gasparo» is probable and is not settled** — at this filming's ceiling the capital will not separate from a C. **The negative is settled.** His age, thirty-two, is right.
how: Work-list row 58. The two surnames were cropped from the same leaf and set side by side.
why: **It thinned a crowd that was being used as an argument.** This archive has been counting the Cioffi on strada Camellara — «*a further Cioffi on the Falco street, alongside Vincenzo Cioffi the vinivendolo, Luca Cioffi the sartore and Giovanni Cioffi*» — as evidence of how thoroughly the two families were mixed. **One of those Cioffi was never a Cioffi.**

what: Nicola Morgillo's dead son was Pasquale, not Raffaele — and the age beside him was never in the act
was: «*34 in 1828, contadino. Husband of Maria Majone; their eight-year-old **RAFFAELE** died in May (atto 14).*» Arienzo Morti 1828, `an_ua14330` img10L.
now: «*è morto nella sua propria casa **PASCALE MORGILLO, d'anni otto***» — **PASQUALE**, in the Neapolitan spelling the clerk uses. And Nicola is **THIRTY-TWO**, from the only act of that year that ages him at all.
how: Work-list row 58, the eleventh volume. Act 14 was read end to end; so was act 56, which is where the thirty-two is written — «*di anni trentadue*», magnified.
why:
**The age had no source.** Atto 14 was cited for «34 in 1828» and **atto 14 gives him no age**: he appears in it as the dead boy's father, and fathers are not aged in these acts.

**It is the second time in one morning that a number was attached to a man from an act that never states it.** The first was Giovanni Cioffi's «forty in 1840», in a death act where he is likewise only the father. **Both came from reading a household into an act instead of reading the act**, and both had a conclusion resting on them.

The same act's other declarant, **VINCENZO MORGILLO**, is **twenty-seven** in May 1828, not twenty-nine — and his wife is **FELICELLA** Rivetti, not Felicetta.

what: Vincenza Vece was Vincenza Pepe, and a household was named after the misreading
was: A household «**Biagio Morgillo & VINCENZA VECE** (strada Nuova di San Gaetano)», from the death act of their twenty-six-month-old daughter Clementina: «*figlia di BIAGIO MORGILLO, di professione contadino, e di **VINCENZA VECE***». Arienzo Morti 1828 act 11, `an_ua14330` img7R.
now: «*e di **VINCENZA PEPE***» — two tall **p** descenders, and nothing resembling a **V**. The household is now **Biagio Morgillo & Vincenza Pepe**.
how: Work-list row 58. The surname was magnified before the household was renamed.
why: **Everything else in that act verified exactly** — twenty-six months, the fourteenth of March, and the two declarants **ANTONIO MORGILLO, 27** and **SIMONE MORGILLO, 24**, both «parente della defunta» on strada San Gaetano. **The one word that was wrong is the one the household was named after**, which is how a misreading gets a URL, a page and a place in the index.

what: «Cossi» survived in the prose of the very act whose household had been corrected to Cioffi
was: «*atto 54, on the death of **Mariantonia COSSI**, seven months, daughter of **Francesco COSSI** and Maria Falco*» — inside the evidence for Giuseppe Falco's appearance as «PARENTE DELLA DEFUNTA» on 24 October 1828.
now: **MARIANTONIA CIOFFI**, daughter of **FRANCESCO CIOFFI** and **MARIA FALCO** — both surnames carrying the double-f ligature, verified from the image.
how: Work-list row 58, while verifying the citation.
why:
**This archive already knew.** The household was corrected to **Francesco Cioffi & Maria Falco** months ago, and a rule was written into `check_corrections.py` specifically to hold «Cossi» out of it. **The rule reads the PERSON fields and not the prose**, so the retired reading went on standing in the evidence string beside the corrected name, in the same file, on the same page.

**A gate that checks names does not check sentences**, and this archive keeps most of what it knows in sentences.

**The act also states the kinship twice, which had not been recorded**: the second declarant, **CESARE CIOFFI, thirty-one**, of the same street, is «Parente della Defunta» as well.

**A GATE FOR THIS WAS WRITTEN AND TAKEN OUT THE SAME HOUR, AND THE REASON IS WORTH MORE THAN THE GATE WAS.** It stripped every «…» quotation out of the evidence — because a quotation may legitimately spell a name the retired way, that being what the document says — and looked for the retired reading in the archive's own words around it.

**It caught this one. It also raised eight false alarms, and six of them were the archive's own withdrawals saying so**: sentences like «*the strada Camellara household is CIOFFI, **not Cossi***». A seventh was a different family altogether, **the Cossi of strada Cossi**, correctly named in the same volume.

**The house style and the gate cannot both exist.** This archive leaves a correction standing beside the thing it corrected, on purpose, because a quietly swapped reading is how archives lie. **To a regular expression, a visible withdrawal is indistinguishable from a correction that never happened.** Narrowing it — flag only when the right reading is absent from the same sentence — still failed on the strada Cossi family, and every narrowing is one more rule nobody will remember.

**So the prose is not checked, and this is the hole, stated.** It is written into `check_corrections.py` where the next person to have the idea will find it before spending the hour.

what: A correction that was nearly published and is wrong: three baptism quotations are real
was:
Nothing was published. **This entry records a withdrawal that was about to happen and did not**, because the archive's policy is that a false correction impugns work that was right, and the near-miss is as instructive as the hit.

While verifying `an_ua14428` (Arienzo births 1831) for work-list row 58, the three Carfora birth acts each carried a quotation of this shape: «*il Sacramento del Battesimo è stato amministrato a **ANTONIO CARFORA** nel giorno **dieci Gennajo** corrente anno*». Read down as far as the usual rendering band goes, the second column of those acts is nothing but the printed formula about the parish returning the *notamento*, **and it never names the child**. The quoted words «il Sacramento del Battesimo è stato amministrato» are also the column's printed HEADING. **It looked exactly like three fabricated quotations**, of the same kind found that morning in the 1840 register.
now: **They are real, and verbatim.** Lower down the same column, past where the band stopped: «*… del controscritto atto di nascita, in piè del quale ha indicato, che il **Sacramento del Battesimo è stato amministrato a ANTONIO CARFORA** — — — nel giorno **Dieci Gennajo corrente***».
how: By rendering the rest of the column before writing anything. The whole volume then verified without a single error — ages, names, streets, dates and both columns of all three acts.
why:
**A band is not a page.** This archive already has that rule, and it was nearly broken from inside an audit whose entire purpose is to stop exactly this.

**The asymmetry is the point.** A missed error leaves a wrong statement standing. **A false correction destroys a true one and puts a slur on the work that made it** — and it does so with all the authority of a corrections page. That is why the withdrawal was checked before it was written, and why the non-event is published here instead of being quietly dropped.

what: SANZONE was SANSONE, and the surname this archive called new was one it already had
was: A household «**Gennaro Morgillo & Maria Felicia SANZONE**», from the marriage act of 2 February 1845, with the note: «*SANZONE **HAD NEVER APPEARED IN THIS ARCHIVE AT ALL** before 15 September 2026*».
now: **SANSONE.** The letter is a long **ſ**, not a **z**.
how: Work-list row 58, and the test is on the same leaf. **«Crescenzo», in the groom's own name four lines above, contains a z**: a compact loop that drops below the line with **no ascender**. The letter in this surname **rises above the x-height before it descends**, which is what a long ſ does in this hand and what a z never does.
why:
**It was not a new surname.** **ANGELO SANSONE**, contadino of **strada Camellara**, declared the death of **MARIA FALCO**, wife of Alfonso Diglio and daughter of Pasquale Falco, on 25 April 1826 — on the Falco's own street, in a register this archive had already read. **The «new surname» was a misreading of one it was holding.**

**Three acts now agree** — 1826, 1843 and 1845 — and that is what turned the 1843 «Sompone» into Sansone as well. **The same wrong letter had been read three different ways in three files**: Sompone, Sanzone, and nothing at all.

**One thing in the same act was nearly "corrected" and is right.** The groom is «**maggiore** di anni venticinque», and «maggiore di anni X» can be a statement of legal majority rather than of age — on which reading the act would not date his birth at all, and this archive's conclusion from it would be void. **The bride, four lines below, is «maggiore di anni VENTITRE». No age of majority is twenty-three.** So «maggiore» is a status, the number is the age, and the inference stands. **The control was inside the same sentence.**

what: Fortunato Crisci's death is act 6, not act 5 — the number in the margin is the folio
was: The two-day-old **FORTUNATO CRISCI**, son of **ARCANGELO CRISCI** and **ANNA FALCO** of strada Camellara, died 24 January 1820 — cited here as `an_ua14322` **img5R act 5**.
now: The leaf is headed «*Numero d'ordine **SEI***». **The act is 6.**
how: Work-list row 58, the fourteenth volume. The word was magnified.
why:
**The trap is in the volume's own layout.** In the 1820 death register the figure stamped in the margin is the **FOLIO**, not the act: folio 5 carries act 6, and folio 25 carries act 47. **Any volume where the stamp happens to match the act teaches the reader a habit that this one breaks.**

**Everything else in both acts of this volume verifies word for word**, including the one this archive leans on hardest: «*è morta nella sua propria casa **ANNA FALCO di anni VENTICINQUE**, moglie di **ARCANGELO CRISCI** … figlia di **PASCALE FALCO** … e di **CHIARA RIVETTI***», with **neither parent marked «defunto»**.

what: Antonia di Guida has a stated age, and this archive had never taken it
was: Nothing was wrong. **This is an addition, recorded here because of what it is an age FOR.** Antonia di Guida — generation four's wife, mother of Crescenzo Falco — is a woman whose **death has never been found**, whose latest dated sighting is her son's marriage on 2 February 1845, and for whom this archive held **no age at all**.
now: Arienzo Nati 1824, act 26, `an_ua14421` img28L: «*che lo stesso è nato da **ANTONIA DI GUIDA** sua moglie legittima, **di anni QUARANTA***». **Forty on 11 March 1824, so born about 1784** — which makes her about sixty-one when Crescenzo married.
how: Work-list row 58. The act was already cited by this archive **three times**, for the child Clemente Falco, for his father Giuseppe Falco and for the birth date. **The mother's age was in the same sentence and was never read off.**
why:
**A citation verified is not a document read.** This row exists to check that what the archive says a document says is what it says — and the commonest thing it has found is not a wrong word but an unread one. **The act had been opened three times.**

The same act gives **GIUSEPPE FALCO at forty-eight and MASSARO on strada Camellara** — born about 1776, against the fifty-six and *possidente* of October 1828 and the forty-six of August 1826. **Three ages, three trades, four years.**

what: Valerio Carfora was alive, and his name was never illegible — it was split across two lines
was: A person called «**[?]erio Carfora**», entered as **dead before 20 January 1860**, with this note: «*MARIA ANTONIA CARFORA'S FATHER — a CARFORA OF ARIENZO, contadino, **dead before January 1860**. **HIS FORENAME DOES NOT RESOLVE**: the word reads «[L/t]erio» at four times magnification and is **left unread rather than guessed***». The quotation given for him was «*figlia di **fu [?]ERIO CARFORA***».
now:
**VALERIO CARFORA, and he was living.** The act reads «*figlia di **VALERIO CARFORA**, di professione **contadino**, domiciliato **ivi***» — **and there it stops**. It writes «defunto» after Carmine Annecchino, «defunta» after Rosa Ceglia, «defunta» after Pasqua Morgillo, and **nothing after him**.

**The act says so a second time.** Item **6** of the eight documents read into the marriage is «*Nel **CONSENSO DEL PADRE** della stessa, **dato nell'atto***». **The bride's father consented in person, in the act.**
how: Work-list row 58, reading the act end to end instead of the sentence that had been quoted from it.
why:
**Two failures, and the second caused the first.**

**The «fu» was never in the document.** This archive's quotation reads «*fu CARMINE ANNECCHINO … fu ROSA CEGLIA … fu [?]ERIO CARFORA … fu PASQUA MORGILLO*» — four times, inside quotation marks. **The act uses «fu» nowhere.** It writes «defunto» and «defunta» AFTER the name, and it writes them **three times, not four**. **Reading a formula into a document instead of off it turned a living man into a dead one**, and the quotation marks made the mistake unchallengeable.

**The forename was not illegible. It was split.** The line ends «*figlia di **Va***» and the next begins «***lerio** Carfora*». This archive magnified the second half of a word and declared the whole of it unreadable — **which is the honest failure mode of a good rule applied to the wrong object.** No other Italian forename ends in *-lerio*.

**What it changes.** The Carfora of Arienzo are no longer a family known only by two dead parents: **Valerio Carfora, contadino, was living at Arienzo on 21 January 1860.** He is a man to look for in the death registers after that date, not before it — and work-list row 63 was searching the wrong side of the line.

what: The Annecchino marriage is of 21 January 1860, not the twentieth
was: **SABBATINO ANNECCHINO × MARIA ANTONIA CARFORA**, Arienzo marriages 1860 act 3 — dated **20 January 1860** in seven places.
now: «*il dì **VENTUNO** di **Gennajo***» — **21 January 1860**. The church celebration followed on the **22nd**.
how: Work-list row 58. The day word was magnified: «ventuno», not «venti».
why:
Small, and it travels: the date was the key on six other people's rows, all of them in the **Annecchino line** this family descends from.

Two more readings in the same act. The groom writes himself **SABBATINO**, with two b. And the second witness is **CRISCI**, not «Crispi» — there is no descender in the word. **How the clerk's three lines divide into two witnesses is not certain** and is left as it reads.

what: The 1860 marriage lists its own dossier, and it names a generation this archive does not have
was: The Annecchino line was held from this marriage act and its children. **Nothing recorded what documents the marriage was built on.**
now: **The act lists all eight**, in the clerk's hand: 1. the groom's **birth act**; 2. his **father's death act**; 3. his **mother's death act**; 4. **the death act of his PATERNAL GRANDFATHER**; 5. the bride's **birth act**; 6. **her father's consent, given in the act**; 7. her **mother's death act**; 8. the **notifications** posted at both domiciles, showing no opposition.
how: Work-list row 58, by reading past the part of the act that had been quoted.
why:
**Item 4 is a generation.** The groom's paternal grandfather — the father of Carmine Annecchino of Forchia — is a man this archive has never named, and **his death act was read aloud at Arienzo on 21 January 1860** and filed with the marriage.

**Item 5 dates the bride exactly**: Maria Antonia Carfora, twenty-nine and born at Arienzo, has a birth act of about 1831 in a register this archive has not read. **Item 7 is Pasqua Morgillo's death**, which would give the Carfora–Morgillo marriage a terminus.

**All of it is in one bundle** — the *processetti* for Arienzo, 1860 — and this archive has read exactly one bundle out of three hundred and twenty. **The eight-item list is what a processetto is for**, and it is now on the work list as row 77.

what: Giovanni Morgillo was «fu PASCALE», not «fu Raffaele» — and «fu» here is a patronymic, not a death mark
was: At Carmine Rivetti's death of 15 September 1821 (`an_ua14323` img23R act 43): «*Declared by Marcello Rivetti, 36, of the same street, and **GIOVANNI MORGILLO FU RAFFAELE**, 45, «parente del defunto»*».
now: «*e **GIOVANNI MORGILLO fu PASCALE**, di anni quarantacinque, di professione contadino, domiciliato ivi **strada Cioffi**, **Parente del Defunto***». The word has a long **ſ** in the middle and ends **-ale**; **Raffaele** carries a double-f and ends **-ele**.
how: Work-list row 58, the seventeenth volume. The word was magnified.
why:
**The patronymic is the only thing that tells one Giovanni Morgillo from another**, and this archive holds several Morgillo houses it cannot yet separate. It also hands over a father: **a PASQUALE MORGILLO, dead by September 1821**, whose son was born about 1776.

**And the act is a lesson in the word «fu» that this archive needed in the same week.** Here «fu» is a **patronymic on a living man** — *Giovanni Morgillo, son of the late Pascale*. **It is not the death mark in a filiation clause.** These forms write that as «**Defunto**» AFTER the parent's name, as this same act does twice, for **NICOLA RIVETTI Defunto** and **ANNA DI RUGGIO Defunta**. **Confusing the two is what buried Valerio Carfora on the 1860 page**, and the correction and the proof are eleven volumes apart in the same register series.

Also recovered: **MARCELLO RIVETTI** is of **strada Monticello de' Cappuccini**, and Giovanni Morgillo of **strada Cioffi** — streets this archive had not taken from the act.

what: A second demonstration that the ages are guessed, and it is sharper than the first
was: This archive's standing demonstration is **GIUSEPPE FALCO, forty on 2 April 1825 and forty-five on 6 April 1825** — five years in four days, in one volume, in one hand.
now: **The same volume does it again with a different man.** **ANIELLO DIGLIO**, contadino of strada Camellara, is «*di anni **quarantasei***» in act 17 of **2 April 1825** and «*di anni **cinquanta***» in act 34 of **19 June 1825**. **Four years in seventy-eight days.**
how: Work-list row 58, verifying `an_ua14327` (Arienzo deaths 1825). Both acts read from the image at full resolution.
why:
**The first demonstration could be read as one clerk's slip on one page.** Two men, two pairs of acts, eleven weeks apart in the same register cannot. **The ages in these volumes are not data. They are the declarant's guess, written down.**

It matters because this archive has repeatedly reasoned from a stated age to a birth year, and then from that birth year to an identification. **That chain is only ever as good as a guess**, and where an identification rests on ages agreeing within a year or two, **it rests on nothing.** Where one rests on ages disagreeing, the disagreement is not evidence either.

The same three acts also give **GIUSEPPE FALCO as MASSARO on 2 April 1825 and CONTADINO on 19 June 1825**. **The trade drifts as freely as the age.**

what: Two brothers were standing in the act and this archive had recorded neither
was: The **«Diversi» act of 1825** — the one that found **CRESCENZO CRISCI** dead in a masseria at Nola and gave this archive a whole Crisci household — was published with its dead man, his widow, his parents and his four surviving children. **Nothing was recorded about who declared it.**
now:
**The two declarants are his brothers, and the act says so in the word this archive insists on magnifying.** «*sono comparsi **DOMENICO CRISCI GERMANO DEL DEFUNTO**, d'anni **quarantanove**, di professione **colono** … domiciliato nel Comune di **ARIENZO** … luogo detto **FABRICA**, e **GABRIELE CRISCI GERMANO** [del Defunto]*».

**«Germano» is full brother.** So **ALESSANDRO CRISCI and CARMINA SORRINO had at least three sons**: Crescenzo, born about 1772; **DOMENICO, born about 1776**; and **GABRIELE**.
how: Work-list row 58, the eighteenth volume. Both «germano» were magnified before anything was written.
why:
**The act was read for the family it buried and not for the family it named.** Everything about the dead man, his wife, his parents and his children was taken off this leaf correctly — and **the first two names on it, standing in the first line, were left where they were.**

**GABRIELE'S AGE IS NOT PUBLISHED, BECAUSE IT CANNOT BE READ.** His line runs into the binding at the right edge, which on this filming is in shadow; his age and trade are inside it. **A first reading of this page had «d'anni trentuno» for him — that was the reader's eye filling a gap, and it is not in the image.** It is recorded here because the near-miss is the point: **the shadow at the gutter is where this archive will invent things if it is not careful.**

what: Maria Rosa Crisci was Maria Crisci — the second name was her surname
was: The youngest of Crescenzo Crisci's four surviving children, published as «*e **MARIA ROSA** d'anni CINQUE*» and carried on this site as **MARIA ROSA CRISCI**.
now: «*Carmina d'anni dieci, e **MARIA CRISCI** d'anni cinque*» — **there is no *Rosa* in the act.** The clerk closes the list of children by giving the last one the family surname, and **this archive read the surname as a second forename.**
how: Work-list row 58. The line was magnified.
why: **It is a small error of a kind that makes a person unfindable.** A search of any index for *Maria Rosa Crisci* born about 1820 at Arienzo returns nothing, and the child it is looking for is filed under *Maria*. **Everything else in the list — Aniello at fifteen, Sante at twelve, Carmina at ten — verifies exactly**, as does the standing warning attached to it: **the list is of MINORS and not of children**, so it is not a complete family.

what: Five citations into the 1832 register, five errors — and two of them pointed at other families
was: Arienzo Morti 1832, `an_ua14334`. **GIOVANNA FALCO**, «*d'anni **SETTANTA**, moglie di **ANTONIO SETT[EMBRE]***», daughter of Michele Falco and **VINCENZA ESPOSITO**, born about **1762**, cited at **img20L act 32**. And **CARMINA FALCO**, six months old, cited at **img48R act 80**.
now:
**GIOVANNA FALCO, «d'anni SESSANTA, moglie di ANTONIO LETTIERI»**, daughter of Michele Falco and **VINCENZA SPOSITO**, born about **1772** — at **img21L act 32**.

**CARMINA FALCO is ACT 81, on IMAGE 49 RIGHT.**
how: Work-list row 58, the twenty-first volume. Every leaf was opened and read.
why:
**Both citations sent a reader to a different family.** Image 20 left is **act 30**: Michele Morgillo, four years old, son of Nicola Morgillo and Elisabetta Crisci. Image 48 right is **act 79**: **DON FRANCESCANTONIO GESSI, seventy-eight, PROPRIETARIO**, widower of Donna Maria Giuseppa Cinque — a gentry household with nothing to do with a six-month-old girl.

**And the readings themselves were a decade and a name out.** «*ſeſſanta*» is written with two long **ſ** and no crossed **tt**; **sixty, not seventy**, which moves her birth from about 1762 to about **1772**. Her husband is **ANTONIO LETTIERI**. Her mother is **SPOSITO**, with no initial E — the form this archive already holds for the Sposito of strada Camellara, and a different name from *Esposito*, which is the foundling name.

**The evidence for this volume was written in a hand this archive can recognise in itself**: five terse, unformatted lines, no quotation, no magnification, no act quoted in the original. **It was harvested and never read.** Every other volume checked in this row was read at least once; this one was not, and it is the only one where every single citation failed.

what: Donn'Anna Quotolo's mother was not «d'Isteria», and the archive now says what it can and cannot read
was: «*figlia di SILVESTRO QUOTOLO Defunto, di professione POSSIDENTE, e di **Maria d'Isteria(?)** Defunta*» — Arienzo Morti 1824 act 20, `an_ua14326` img16L, with the question mark this archive puts on a word it has not settled.
now: **«d'ISTERIA» IS EXCLUDED.** At the leaf's full resolution the word plainly ends **-ustina** — there is no **r** before the last syllable — and it begins **Di**. **The likeliest reading is MARIA DI GIUSTINA**, an attested Campanian surname.
how: Work-list row 58. The word was magnified at the filming's ceiling.
why:
**The middle letter will not separate a g from an f**, so *Difustina* cannot be ruled out, and the positive reading is **published as likely and not as settled**. **The negative is settled**, and that is worth publishing on its own: a reader searching for a *d'Isteria* at Arienzo is searching for a name that is not in this act.

Everything else in that volume verified exactly, including the act this archive had to correct once before: «*PASCALE FALCO, di anni cinquantacinque, COLONO … **ZIO del Defunto**, e GIUSEPPE FALCO, di anni quarantadue, COLONO … **ZIO del Defunto***». **Both «zio», both magnified, both right.** One small fidelity note: the manuscript writes **PASCALE**, and this archive's quotation modernises it to «PASQUALE» inside the guillemets.

what: Maria Rosa Falco was twenty-two months old, not sixteen years
was: «*Maria Rosa Falco, **d'anni SEDICI**, contadina, figlia di Michele Falco, contadino*» — Arienzo Morti 1834, 30 May, cited at `an_ua14336` img23R.
now: «*è morta nella sua propria casa **MARIA ROSA FALCO, di mesi VENTIDUE**, nata in Arienzo … figlia di **MICHELE FALCO** … e di **ANTONIA VIGLIOTTA**, domiciliata ivi*» — **IMAGE 24 RIGHT**. **Twenty-two months.** Born about July 1832.
how: Work-list row 58, the twenty-second volume. «*di **mesi** ventidue*» was magnified before anything was changed.
why:
**A sixteen-year-old contadina and an infant of not quite two are not the same kind of person.** Everything a reader might have built on the first — a birth about 1818, a working girl, a daughter of marriageable age, a candidate for any Maria Rosa Falco marrying in the 1830s — **is wrong, and wrong in a way that invites false matches rather than blocking them.**

**Her mother was never recorded**: **ANTONIA VIGLIOTTA**, named in the act. And she opens a question this archive will not settle by guessing — **the Michele Falco who buries a son in 1842 is married to an ANTONIA MIGLIORE**. Same forename, same town, same trade, eight years apart. **Either one of the two surnames is misread, or there are two Michele Falco each married to an Antonia.**

**And the citation pointed at the wrong leaf**: image 23 right is Carmina Zimbardo, fourteen days old.

what: A citation withdrawn: the leaf cited for Anna Falco holds a different child
was: Two rows for an **ANNA FALCO, eight days old, daughter of MICHELANGELO FALCO**, dead **7 March 1834**, both cited at `an_ua14336` img10L.
now:
**Image 10 left is MARIA PORRINO**, eight days old, daughter of Angelo Porrino and Pasqua Rivetti, dead on **8** March 1834.

**The citation is withdrawn. The person is not.**
how: Work-list row 58. Five leaves were opened around it: image 8 right, Gelsomina Ditto, 21 February; image 9 left, Carmela Zimbardo, 24 February; image 9 right, Francesco Liparulo, **7 March** — the only act of that day on these leaves; image 10 left, Maria Porrino; image 10 right, Flavia Zimbardo, 14 March. **No Anna Falco among them.**
why:
**The same age and all but the same day.** An eight-day-old girl dead on the 8th of March, and an eight-day-old girl dead on the 7th — **that is how a mis-indexed record becomes a person.** And **MICHELANGELO FALCO**, the father this archive gives her, is a forename that appears **nowhere else in this archive**, in any register, at any date.

**She is not deleted, because the archive does not delete on suspicion.** She may be real and filed elsewhere in a volume of ninety acts. But **a citation that sends a reader to somebody else is worse than no citation**, because it looks like proof. **Locating or retiring her is work-list row 78.**

**FOUND THE SAME DAY, AND THE WITHDRAWAL IS SUPERSEDED — SEE THE ENTRY BELOW.** A contact-sheet sweep of the volume's name lines put her on **image 11 left**, and the leaf was then read. **She is real.** She died on **16 March 1834**, not the 7th, and her mother is **RAFFAELA FALCO**, not Mariantonia Vigliotta. **The withdrawal stands as written because it was right when it was written**: the citation did not hold, and saying so is what made the sweep happen.

what: Anna Falco found: act 16, 16 March 1834 — and her mother is RAFFAELA FALCO
was: An **ANNA FALCO, eight days old, dead 7 March 1834**, daughter of **MICHELANGELO FALCO** and **MARIANTONIA VIGLIOTTA**, entered twice, cited at `an_ua14336` img10L — a leaf that holds **MARIA PORRINO**, eight days old, dead on the **8th** of March. The citation had been withdrawn as unverified earlier the same day.
now:
«*il dì **SEDICI** del mese di **MARZO** … è morta nella sua propria casa **ANNA FALCO, di giorni OTTO** … figlia di **MICHELANGELO FALCO**, di professione contadino, domiciliato ivi, e di **RAFFAELA FALCO**, domiciliata ivi*» — **act 16, image 11 LEFT**, declared by **GIUSEPPE CARFORA, forty** and **TOMASO SPOSITO, sixty**, both of **strada Camellara**.

**She died on the SIXTEENTH, not the seventh. Her mother is RAFFAELA FALCO, not Mariantonia Vigliotta. And she is not this couple's child.**
how: **A contact-sheet sweep of the volume's own name lines** — thirty-two tiles across sixteen leaves, one band of each half-page — put her on image 11 left in a single request. **The leaf was then rendered and read at full resolution**, because a contact sheet may produce a candidate and never a record.
why:
**Everything about her that was published was wrong except her name and her eight days.** The leaf, the day, the mother, and the household.

**Her mother is a FALCO MARRIED TO A FALCO, and this archive had never recorded her.** Whether she is the **RAFFAELA FALCO** married to a **FRANCESCO FALCO**, who buried a six-month-old Carmina fourteen months earlier, is **left open**: either there are two Raffaela Falco married to two Falco men — which this family's habits make entirely possible, four Maria Falco having already had to be separated — or one woman was widowed and remarried inside fourteen months. **The child is published where the document puts her and the question is published beside her.**

**The old row is left standing in the Vigliotta household as a withdrawal rather than deleted**, so that anyone who found her there once can see what happened to her.

what: «Antonia Migliore» never existed — she is ANTONIA VIGLIOTTA, and a household is merged
was: A household «**Michele Falco & ANTONIA MIGLIORE**», built from Arienzo Morti 1842 act 55, the death of their two-year-old **MATTEO FALCO** on strada Camellara — «*figlio di MICHELE FALCO … e di **ANTONIA MIGLIORE***».
now: «*e di **ANTONIA VIGLIOTTA**, domiciliata ivi*». **The household is merged into MICHELE FALCO & ANTONIA VIGLIOTTA.**
how: Work-list row 58. The word was cropped from the 1842 act and set beside the same clerk's **«Antonia Vigliotta»** in the death act of **MARIA ROSA FALCO** of 30 May 1834 — **the same capital V, the same «gli» with its tall l, the same «-otta»**. Migliore has no V and no double t.
why:
**The marriage register settles it from the other end.** On **12 February 1850** **MICHELE FALCO, forty-three, colono of strada Camellara**, marries **GIOVANNA D'AMBROGIO** as «***VEDOVO DI ANTONIA VIGLIOTI***». **One wife, one surname, three acts — 1834, 1842 and 1850** — and this archive had been keeping her in two households under two names.

**It also answers an open question raised earlier the same day.** Verifying the 1834 register had turned up a *Michele Falco × Antonia Vigliotta* against the *Michele Falco × Antonia Migliore* of 1842, and the question published then was whether one surname was misread or there were two couples. **It was one surname, misread once.**

**What is NOT merged, and why.** This archive also holds a **MICHELANGELO FALCO × MARIANTONIA VIGLIOTTA**, married December 1828, entered as a son of **PASQUALE Falco and Chiara Rivetti**. **The 1850 act makes Michele Falco a son of RAFFAELE FALCO and a different CHIARA RIVETTI, a filatrice.** Two men, two fathers, and two wives who share a surname and very nearly a forename. **They are left apart**, and the coincidence is recorded rather than resolved.

what: Every citation into the 1836 register was off by one leaf, in the same direction
was: Five citations into Arienzo Morti 1836 (`an_ua14338`), written as **p11, p17, p29** and **p32** — a numbering this archive uses nowhere else.
now: **Images 12, 18, 30 and 33, all RIGHT halves.** Every one is **exactly one higher** than the number recorded, and none of the four recorded which half of the leaf.
how: Work-list row 58. The leaves cited were opened first and held other families — image 11 is a Sanfone infant and a Francesco di Mazzo; image 17 a Filomena Crisci and an Alessandro Lettieri. **Two contact-sheet sweeps of the volume's name lines, thirty-eight and forty-two tiles, then found all four Falco in two requests.**
why:
**A constant offset is a fingerprint.** One wrong leaf is a slip; four wrong leaves all off by one, in one volume, means **the numbers were copied from something that counts differently** — a viewer's page counter, or a list that starts at zero. **They were never checked against an image.**

The evidence written from them shows it too: five terse lines, no quotation, no magnification, no act number — **the same hand this row found in the 1832 and 1834 volumes.** **Where the citation format is unusual, the reading behind it usually is not a reading.**

what: Margarita Falco's husband and mother were both wrong, and Pasqualina Falco was six months old, not ten
was: **MARGARITA FALCO**, sixty, «moglie di **Domenico [Crisci]**» — the surname in brackets, as a guess — daughter of Francesco Falco defunto and **«Maria Angela ULIVIECCIO»**. And **PASQUALINA FALCO**, «di mesi **DIECI**», daughter of a Francesco Falco of strada Camellara.
now: «*moglie di **DOMENICO COSPI** … figlia di FRANCESCO FALCO Defunto … e di **MARIANGELA IULIUCCIO** Defunta*». And «*PASQUALINA FALCO, di mesi **SEI**, … figlia di **FRANCESCO FALCO** … e di **RAFFAELA FALCO***».
how: Work-list row 58, once the leaves were found. Both surnames magnified; **«Cospi» wraps to the next line**, which is how it came to be guessed at rather than read.
why:
**The bracket was honest and the guess was wrong, and that combination is the most dangerous thing on a page.** «Domenico [Crisci]» says *we did not read this* and then supplies a name anyway, and a reader in a hurry keeps the name and drops the bracket. **The act says COSPI.**

**«Ulivieccio» has a v and an e that are not in the word**, which reads **IULIUCCIO**, after a single forename **MARIANGELA**.

**And naming Pasqualina's mother joined two households this archive was holding apart from itself.** **RAFFAELA FALCO** makes her a sister of the **CARMINA FALCO** buried at six months in December 1832 — one couple, two stubs. The same thing happened to **SALVATORE FALCO**: his mother is **MARIANTONIA VIGLIOTTA**, which puts him in the household of the **MICHELE FALCO of strada Camellara** whose other children were already here. **Two «unjoined» households in this volume were not families at all. They were lines nobody had read.**

what: A marriage this archive dated from one document is now dated by a second that never met it
was: **CARMINE ANTONIO FALCO married GIOVANNA ARRICALE on 18 November 1872 at Arienzo** — a date this archive held from **one** source, the 1897 marriage dossier of their son Raffaele, which quotes it.
now: **Her own birth act carries it in the margin.** Arienzo Nati 1848, act 114, `an_ua14445` img115R–116L: «*A **18 Novembre 1872** l'Uff.le dello Stato Civ.le d'**ARIENZO** sposò **GIOVANNA ARRICOLA** con **CARMINE ANTONIO FALCO***», annotated at Caserta in 1884.
how: Work-list row 58, verifying the citations into the 1848 birth register. **The act had been read before and the margin had not.**
why:
**Nothing changes and that is the point.** Two documents written twenty-five years apart, in two towns, by two hands, give the same day for the same marriage — and this archive had been resting it on one.

**It is also this archive's own method catching something it had walked past.** The rule that a civil birth act can carry the child's marriage in its margin was written here from the 1819 act of Domenico Clemente Falco. **The act was opened, the parents were read off it, and the margin was left**, which is the same failure as the «zio» in 1826 and the two brothers in the 1825 Diversi: **the page was read for what it was wanted for.**

The margin spells her **ARRICOLA** where the act writes **ARRICALE**. The act governs, and the variant is recorded rather than silently harmonised.

what: Domenica Falco married twice, and the second margin was on the page the whole time
was: «*THE MARGIN OF HER BIRTH ACT CARRIES HER WEDDING, TWENTY-EIGHT YEARS LATER*» — **10 October 1874**, **DOMENICA FALCO** to **PASQUALANTONIO GUIDA**, written down the left edge of her birth act of 13 September 1846 (`an_ua14443` img71L). **One margin was quoted. There are two.**
now:
In the right-hand column of the same page, below the registrar's signature: «*(1) **A 25 Marzo 1881** l'Uff.le dello Stato Civ.le d'**ARIENZO** sposò **DOMENICA FALCO** con **PASQUALE SACCAVINO** — **Caserta 16 Giugno 1884***».

**She married twice**, and **PASQUALANTONIO GUIDA died between October 1874 and March 1881**.
how: Work-list row 58, re-reading the whole leaf instead of the margin that had been quoted from it.
why:
**One birth act now carries two marriages, thirty-five years and twenty-eight years after it was written, in a series Antenati stops filming in 1865.** That is the strongest demonstration this archive has of its own margin method — and it is also the fourth time in one day that **a page was read for what it was wanted for and the rest of it left**: the «zio» in the 1826 act, the two brothers in the 1825 Diversi, the 1872 marriage in Giovanna Arricale's margin, and now this.

**The two annotations were dated at Caserta seven weeks apart in 1884**, which is when the province went through the registers adding them. **They were written by the same clerk, on the same page, at the same time.**

what: Luigi Falco's death is act 91 — «47» was the figure stamped on the leaf
was: The death of **LUIGI FALCO**, forty-one, *industriante*, husband of Carolina Cimmino, 16 December 1864 — cited four times as **Arienzo Morti 1864, atto 47**. It is one of this archive's load-bearing acts: it is what shows the register's stated age wrong by three, and it is the sighting that keeps **VINCENZO FALCO** alive at seventy-two.
now: The act is headed «**Num. d'ordine 91**». **47 is the figure stamped in the leaf's margin**, and the facing page of the same opening is «**Num. d'ordine 92**».
how: Work-list row 58. Both pages of the opening were rendered and their headings read.
why:
**Everything the act is relied on for verifies exactly** — «*è morto nella sua casa **LUIGI FALCO = marito di CAROLINA CIMMINO**, nato in Arienzo, di anni **quarantuno**, di professione **INDUSTRIANTE**, domiciliato **Contrada Capodiconca**, figlio di **VINCENZO**, di professione colono, domiciliato **alla Camellara***» — the marriage nobody knew about, the trade, the move off strada Camellara, and the absence of any death mark on either parent.

**Only the number was the leaf's and not the act's.** It is the third volume in this row where a stamped figure was taken for an act number, after the 1820 death register and the 1832 one. **In three different volumes the stamp counts something different, and only the manuscript heading says which.**

One quotation is tightened too: the act writes «**ANDREA CRISCI**», dropping the *-na*, where this archive quoted «ANDREANA CRISCI» inside the guillemets.

what: Andreana Crisci's brother has a name: LORENZO ANTONIO
was: A person entered as «**[son] Crisci**», born 1817, with this note: «*The child's given name is further down the act and was **NOT REACHED** in this pass*». Arienzo Nati 1817, `an_ua14414` img33L.
now: «*a cui si è dato il nome di **LORENZO ANTONIO***» — **ACT 63**, born **1 September 1817** at eighteen hours, declared the same day by **ARCANGELO CRISCI, fifty-two, contadino of STRADA CAMELLARA**, of **SARA RUGGIERO**, forty-five.
how: Work-list row 58, verifying the citation. The whole act was rendered instead of the band that had been read, and the name was magnified.
why:
**The note was honest and it was a promise nobody kept.** «Not reached in this pass» is exactly the right thing to write — and it sat on the page for days while the act it describes was four inches further down the same image.

**He is a brother for ANDREANA CRISCI**, generation three's wife, born when her mother was forty-five and she herself was about twenty-one. The archive already held a sister, **CARMELA CRISCI**, seven days old, dead 9 January 1815. **This household now has three children and one of them has a birth date.**

**The same act carries the clerk's own correction of the year**: 1816 written, struck, and **«diciassette»** put above it — as does act 69, three leaves on.

what: Carlantonio Morgillo and Rosa Falco have a daughter, and she was in an act this archive had already opened
was: A household «**Carlantonio Morgillo & Rosa Falco**» with **no children at all**, built on his age from three sightings and on her being named as his wife at her death in 1830.
now:
Arienzo Nati 1817, **act 69, image 36 left, 22 September 1817**: «*è nata nella sua propria casa … da **ROSA FALCO** sua moglie legittima d'anni **TRENTADUE**, una **Femina** che ci ha presentata … a cui si è dato il nome di **GIOVANNA***».

**GIOVANNA MORGILLO**, and her mother is **thirty-two**, so born about **1785**.
how: Work-list row 58. The act had been cited here for one thing — her husband's age — and read no further.
why:
**The citation was made for a number and the family in the act was left where it was.** That is the fifth time in one day: the «zio» of 1826, the two brothers of the 1825 Diversi, the 1872 margin on Giovanna Arricale's birth act, the second margin on Domenica Falco's, and now a first child for a household that had none.

**It is the same fault every time and it is not a reading fault.** Every one of these acts was found, opened and transcribed correctly as far as it was read. **What failed was stopping.**

what: Two more citations pointed at the wrong leaf, and one of them at a daughter of the founders
was: **ROSA FALCO**, forty-two, wife of Carlantonio Morgillo and **a documented daughter of MATTEO FALCO and FRANCESCA CRISCI**, dead 16 October 1830 — cited at `an_ua14332` **img36R act 53**. And **ANNA FALCO**, thirteen months, dead 4 May 1831 — cited at `an_ua14333` **img19R act 33**.
now: **Image 37 RIGHT** and **image 20 RIGHT.**
how: Work-list row 58. Both cited leaves were opened and held other people — image 36 right is **COSTANZA MAJONE**, sixty, widow of Domenico Papa, dead in the Ospedale di Ave Gratia Plena; image 19 right is **CARMINA MACCANIELLO**, ten months. **Two contact-sheet sweeps of the volumes' own date and name lines found both acts in two requests.**
why:
**Both readings are exactly right and both addresses are wrong**, which is now the commonest shape of error in this audit. Rosa Falco's act verifies word for word, including the part the whole line hangs on: «*figlia di **MATTEO FALCO Defunto** … e di **FRANCESCA CRISCI Defunta***», with the mother's surname passing this archive's own three-way test at magnification — **a narrow shoulder, no round o, no double-f ascender.**

**One more for the age series.** Rosa Falco is **forty-two** in October 1830 and **thirty-two** in her daughter Giovanna's birth act of September 1817. **Ten years in thirteen.**

what: A correction to something published here this morning: Antonia di Guida's two agreeing ages were two guesses
was: Published earlier on **20 September 2026**, on finding her age for the first time: «*Forty on 11 March 1824 … and forty in April 1825 — **two independent statements agreeing**, for a woman this archive had no age for at all this morning*», giving a birth about **1784**.
now: **There is a third and it does not agree.** Arienzo Nati 1818, act 57, `an_ua14415` img47R: «*da **ANTONIA DI GUIDA** sua moglie legittima, d'anni **TRENTA***» — **thirty in June 1818**, which puts her birth about **1788**. **Ten years in six.**
how: Work-list row 58, six hours later, verifying the next volume in the same series.
why:
**The agreement of 1824 and 1825 was the agreement of two guesses, not of two witnesses**, and calling it «two independent statements agreeing» dressed it as corroboration. **Her age is as unreliable as everyone else's in these registers**, and this archive has spent the day proving exactly that about other people.

**It is a correction to a finding a few hours old**, which is the point of checking a find against what is already held in the same pass — **including what was added in that pass.**

The same volume convicts the 1816 register outright. **VINCENZO FALCO and ANDREANA CRISCI are thirty-five and twenty-five in April 1816, and twenty-seven and twenty in May 1818** — he eight years younger and she five, in twenty-five months. **Their baptisms of 1 February 1792 and 30 November 1796 agree with the 1818, 1824 and 1826 acts to within two years, and with 1816 not at all.**

what: The front page's own diagram was audited — and two of the four «errors» were not errors
was:
**David asked whether the home-page figure still matched the research.** It did not, in four places.

**«Adriana Crisci»**, twice, for generation three's wife. **«Giovanna Arricole»**, twice, for generation five's. **«On 25 May 1831 Vincenzo Falco … declared the death of Michelangelo's thirteen-month-old daughter Anna»**. And **«Four Falco households on strada Camellara … Michele · Francesco · a second Michele — NOT joined»**.
now:
**ANDREANA CRISCI.** The name appears **sixty-eight times** in the household file and **«Adriana» not once**; every act read from the image on 20 September 2026 — 1816, 1818, 1824, 1826, 1846, 1861, 1864 — writes **Andreana**.

**GIOVANNA ARRICALE.** Her own birth act of 22 December 1848 writes **ARRICALE** in the body and **ARRICOLA** in the margin. **«Arricole» is a fourth spelling that no document uses.** Her marriage is dated too: **18 November 1872**.

**4 MAY 1831**, act 33, and the act was read from the image: «*sono comparsi **ANDREA CRISCI**, di anni cinquantotto … **VICINO DELLA DEFUNTA**, e **VINCENZO FALCO**, di anni **trentotto** … **PARENTE DELLA DEFUNTA***». **The kinship claim holds exactly. The date was three weeks out.**

**FIVE households, and a second MICHELANGELO.**
how: By opening the four claims against the household file and, where the two disagreed, against the image. Work-list row 58's machinery, turned on the front page instead of on a citation.
why:
**The diagram is the first thing a reader sees and it had not been re-audited since it was drawn.** Three of the four errors are names and dates that the archive's own files already had right — **the figure had drifted from the data behind it**, which is this archive's standing fault in a new place.

**The fourth changed because the research changed today.** There are now **five** Falco households on that street, not four, and one of the new ones is **a second MICHELANGELO** — Michelangelo Falco and **RAFFAELA FALCO**, whose daughter Anna died on 16 March 1834, three years after the Anna of Mariantonia Vigliotta. **The old label said «a second Michele»; it should have said a second Michelangelo, and could not have, because he was found this morning.**

**Checking the front page also caught two faults of my own, both from today**, and they are the fault this session has spent the day documenting: **a correction that stopped halfway**. The household «Francesco Falco & Maria Angela **Ulivieccio**» kept the withdrawn surname **in its name** after the evidence inside it had been corrected to **MARIANGELA IULIUCCIO**; and a one-row stub, «Michele Falco (strada Camellara)», was left standing after the act in it was read and its mother named. **Both are now fixed.**

**And one stale sentence is retired.** The first Raffaele Falco's row still said «*which of the two is generation four is now an open question*». **The very next row in the same household answers it**: he was buried on 28 October 1817, aged about eighteen months. **The Raffaele of 10 May 1818 is generation four, and the archive had known it all along.**

---

**TWO OF THE FOUR WERE WRONG, AND THEY WERE MINE. Corrected the same day, by the audit that was meant to catch drift and caught a false correction instead.**

**«ADRIANA CRISCI» WAS RIGHT.** I reported that the name appears sixty-eight times as ANDREANA in the household file and «Adriana» not once, and concluded the figure named generation three's wife wrongly. **The household file records the CIVIL ACTS, and the civil acts do all say Andreana. Her BAPTISM says Adriana** — and this archive's own line file says so in terms: «*the same bundle holds her baptism extract: **Adriana**, baptised at Arienzo on 30 November 1796 … **Adriana is the name she was given at the font, and it is the root of every variant the registers throw up — Andreana, Andriana, Andrea***». **The figure was naming her by her baptismal name.** It now gives both, as the line file does.

**AND «ARRICOLE» IS ATTESTED.** I wrote that it is «a fourth spelling that no document uses». **The 1814 processetti write it** — «*ANNA **ARRICOLE** di Angelo*» and «*SARA **ARRICOLE**, di Alessandro*». **Giovanna's own birth act does say ARRICALE**, so naming her that is still right; **the reason I gave for it was false.**

**What actually was wrong on the figure: the date of the 1831 act, and the count of Falco households on strada Camellara.** Two of four.

**This is the failure this archive names as the worst kind**: a false correction impugns work that was right, and it does it with the authority of a corrections page. **I checked the household file, found the name absent, and did not check the line file or the baptism.** The rule exists and is written down — *check a find OR A CORRECTION against what is already held, in the same pass* — and I broke it twice in one entry.

what: Matteo Falco the possidente was twenty-three, not twenty-eight — and «Cossi» was still standing in a third place
was:
«*e **MATTEO FALCO**, di anni **VENTOTTO**, di professione **POSSIDENTE** … domiciliato in strada Porta di Sopra*» — Arienzo Morti 1827 act 52, **born about 1799**. He is the only Falco in twenty annual registers called a *possidente*, he carries the founding ancestor's name, and he is unjoined.

And, on a different page, «*declaring atto 30, the death of **Giuseppe COSSI**, aged one, son of **Francesco COSSI***».
now: «*di anni **VENTITRE***» — **twenty-three**, so born about **1804**. And **GIUSEPPE CIOFFI**, son of **FRANCESCO CIOFFI**.
how: Work-list row 58. The age was magnified: the **i** of «ventitre» is dotted and the **tre** is crossed, where «ventotto» would show a round **o** and no dot.
why:
**Five years moves him out of the generation this archive had put him in.** A Falco possidente born about 1799 is of the direct line's generation three; one born about 1804 is not. **Nothing joins him either way** — but an unjoined man is still dated, and this archive had dated him wrong.

**And «Cossi» was found standing in a THIRD place.** The household was corrected to CIOFFI months ago and a gate was written to hold it; the retired reading has now been found surviving in the prose of the 1828 act, of this 1827 act, and in six sentences inside the household itself. **The gate reads person fields. This archive keeps most of what it knows in sentences**, and a prose gate was tried on 20 September and withdrawn because it could not tell a withdrawal from a relapse.

**The act also names a kinsman nobody had recorded**: «*e **CESARE CIOFFI**, di anni trenta … **PARENTE DEL DEFUNTO***», where Giuseppe Falco beside him is only «vicino». **The same Cesare Cioffi is «Parente della Defunta» in 1828 for another child of the same couple**, which is the nearest this archive has come to placing him.

what: Two people were published as «alive» on a signal this archive had itself disproved
was: **GIUSEPPE DI GUIDA**: «*figlio di Giuseppe di Guida» — no «fu», **so alive in October 1817***». **GIUSEPPE MORGILLO**: «*figlio di Giuseppe Morgillo» — no «fu», **so alive in July 1818***». Both flat statements of fact.
now: **WEAK INFERENCE ONLY, on both.** On **14 September 2026** this archive disproved the «quondam» signal for the parish Latin register: **MATTEO FALCO is «filium Matthaei», with no «q.», seventeen days after his own burial.** Civil acts are a different tradition and these two are probably sound — **but they no longer carry the weight those sentences gave them.**
how: **Work-list row 75**, reconciling `data/households.tsv` against `site/src/data/households.json`. **The downgrade had been written into the TSV on 14 September and never into the file the site is built from.**
why:
**The archive stopped believing this six days before it stopped saying it.** That is the same failure as «Pivera» — a correction that reached the file nobody builds from — and it is worse here, because what was left standing is **an argument from silence**, the one kind of reasoning this archive has published a rule against.

**Row 75 is now done, and it found more than two.** Sixty rows disagreed about what the document said. **Thirty-six were the JSON carrying today's verification work and the TSV holding the older text.** **Nine were the TSV holding something the JSON had never had**: these two downgrades; the identification of **the fourth Maria Falco**; that her household «lasted at most a few years»; that **Suor Maria Maddalena Rivetti** is the third sign of a Rivetti house of standing; **why a machine-transcript row of 1841 is deliberately left standing** beside the act; the refusal that **Vigliotti and Vigliotta are not established as one family**; that Domenico Clemente Falco's act is **where the birth-act-margin method came from**; and that Filomena di Lucia's father's *muratore* is a lettered-adjacent trade in a corpus of contadini.

**All nine are now on the site, and the two files agree row for row.**

**AND THE GATE NOW READS THE EVIDENCE.** `check_release.py` compared only who was in which household; it now compares what the document says as well, on whitespace-flattened text, allowing several entries under one key. **Verified by reintroducing the «Pivera» fault, which it refuses with exit 1.** It also prints the warning it has to: **do not bulk-copy — the newer text is not always the longer one**, which is how three corrected readings were nearly destroyed this morning.

what: A citation to a leaf that does not exist, in a volume that does not go that far
was: **DON GIUSEPPE CIOFFI, fifty-six, SACERDOTE**, son of Andrea Cioffi the possidente and Orsola Zimbardo, dead **4 December 1827** — cited as «`an_ua14329` **img47L atto84**», Arienzo Morti 1827.
now: **The volume has FORTY-TWO images and SIXTY-EIGHT acts.** Image 47 does not exist; act 84 does not exist. **The citation is withdrawn.**
how:
Work-list row 58. The render tool reported «an_ua14329 has 42 images; 47 is out of range» — and **earlier attempts on the same leaf had returned 403, which this archive's rule says means «wait», never «missing».** Both were true at once: the service was throttling **and** the leaf was never there. **The rule held and was not enough**: a 403 tells you nothing about whether the page exists, so a citation can hide behind one indefinitely.

The volume was then swept three times: the act number on every leaf from image 30 to 42, and the name line on every act from image 20 to 41. **The last act is 68 and the volume closes with three December deaths — Vincenza Di[?], Antonio Lettieri, Raffaela Zimbardo.** No priest among them.
why:
**The man is not in doubt and the reference is.** His sister **CELIA CIOFFI**'s death act of 3 June 1843 names the same father, the same trade and the same mother, so the household stands on two documents and this is one of them going missing, not the family.
