**What it costs is the thing this row exists to protect.** A citation that cannot be followed is not evidence; it is a claim with a footnote shape. **Where the act was actually read is now unknown** — another year's volume, or an index rather than an act. Row 79.

**It is the second impossible citation found today**, after the one that sent a reader to a Maria Porrino instead of an Anna Falco. **That one was recoverable in a single contact sheet. This one is not.**

what: Where «Gaspare Cossi» came from: the index said Gaspare, the act says Cesare, and neither said Cossi
was: Corrected earlier on **20 September 2026**: the child buried on 9 August 1826 was published as «**Giuseppe COSSI**, son of **GASPARE COSSI** and Maria Sposito», and the act reads «**GIUSEPPE CIOFFI** … figlio di **CESARE CIOFFI** … e di **MARIA SPOSITO**». **What was not known then was where the wrong reading came from.**
now:
**The 1826 tavola alfabetica, entry 56**: «*56. **CIOFFI GIUSEPPE** … [Cioffi] **GASPARE** e **SPOSITO MARIA** … A dì **9 agosto** 1826*».

**The index says GASPARE and the act says CESARE. The index says CIOFFI and the archive published COSSI.**
how: Work-list row 79, reading the death indexes for 1826–1829 at `an_ua14288`–`14291`.
why:
**One error was assembled out of two sources and neither was the act.** The forename came from the index, which is wrong; the surname came from somewhere else again, because the index has it right. **A reading built from two second-hand sources looks exactly like a reading**, and nothing in the citation said which part came from where.

**It is also the plainest evidence yet for a rule this archive already has.** The *tavola* is the clerk's own contact sheet: written fast, from the acts, at the end of a year. **It may produce a candidate and never a record.** Where the index and the act disagree, **the act governs** — and this archive had been quoting the index inside guillemets as though it were the act.

what: Don Giuseppe Cioffi is in none of the four likeliest years, and the negative is bounded
was: Work-list row 79 was raised this morning when the citation for **DON GIUSEPPE CIOFFI, fifty-six, SACERDOTE** turned out to point at a leaf and an act that do not exist. It named 1826, 1828 and 1829 as where to look, beside 1827.
now: **He is in none of them.** The *tavole alfabetiche* for **1826, 1827, 1828 and 1829** were read — `an_ua14288` to `an_ua14291` — and in every one of them **the C leaf was opened**. **There is no Giuseppe Cioffi, Crisci or Cossi described as SACERDOTE in any of the four years.** The only religious in the stretch are **Crisci Suor Maria Teresa**, a *monaca*, in 1827, and the trades otherwise run contadino, calzolajo, sartore, sensale, vetrajo, amanuense, proprietario, gentiluomo.
how: Four index volumes, nine leaves rendered at full page width, the C block read in each.
why:
**A bounded negative is worth as much as a find and this archive publishes them.** Four years are now closed and the next reader does not repeat them.

**What it leaves.** Either the year is wrong by more than two, or **the reading never came from a death act at all** — and the evidence for that is now stronger, because the same four indexes showed that the archive's «Gaspare Cossi» of 1826 was assembled from an index and a machine transcript. **His parents are not in doubt**: his sister CELIA CIOFFI's act of 3 June 1843 names the same father, the same trade and the same mother. **The man stands on his sister's document; it is his own that has gone missing.**

what: The backlog of «unfinished research files» was forty-four, and forty-three of them were finished
was: The work list declared **`unreconciled: 39`** and the coverage gate reported **forty-four outstanding research files with no row against them** — the death of Matteo Falco, the parish marriage indexes, every FindMyPast harvest, the Zampiello of Arpaia, and forty more.
now: **Twenty-three**, all of them genuine, **and every one now covered by a row.** **`unreconciled` is 0.**
how:
Work-list row 74. The account was pointed at **`not complete`**, and `complete` answers a different question — **was this REGISTER read end to end.** A finding file has no reason to contain the word COMPLETE, so all fifty-three of them were counted as unfinished work.

`build_researchlog.py` now writes **`outstanding`** separately: **a file is outstanding when it is a per-volume SWEEP that has not finished.** This archive names those `*-progress.md` — thirty-four of eighty-seven — which is a convention, not a guess.
why:
**A number that is too big is not a safe error.** It hid the one item that mattered inside forty-three that did not — **the Arienzo civil marriage register for 1815, images 17 to 30, never opened.** About twelve marriages, half a year, in the densest kind of volume this archive reads: both spouses, both sets of parents, ages, trades and streets on one leaf. **The read half of that volume already produced the soap-makers of San Felice a Cancello.** It is now row 81.

**The gate was right and the declaration was wrong.** The coverage gate said something was uncounted; it was the archive's own `accounts` block that told it what to count. **A gate can only be as honest as the thing it is pointed at.**

what: Twenty retired readings were still standing across nine pages, and the audit that found them found a false correction of mine
was: After the front-page audit, **every page in the site was grepped for the readings retired on 20 September 2026.** **Twenty were still standing across nine files.**
now: **Fixed**: **VINCENZA SPOSITO** for «Esposito» in four places (`UnderWhoseRule`, `antenati` ×2, `families` ×2); **VINCENZA PEPE** for «Vece» on `morgillo`; **MARIANGELA IULIUCCIO** for «Maria Angela Ulivieccio» on `families` and `open-questions`; **GIOVANNA ARRICALE** for «Arricole» on `lines`, `arienzo` and `name`; and **4 May 1831** in a tooltip attribute on the front-page figure that this morning's fix had missed — **the prose was corrected and the `data-year` beside it was not.**
how: A mechanical grep of `site/src` for eighteen retired→corrected pairs, with the corrections page and the notes excluded, because those two legitimately quote what has been withdrawn.
why:
**The corrections were all made in the data and the pages kept saying the old thing.** That is the fault this archive has spent the day naming in other people's work and committing in its own — **a correction that stops at the file it was written in**. The data files are gated against it now; **the prose pages are not, and cannot easily be**, for the reason the prose gate was withdrawn this morning: **a page that says «X, not Y» looks exactly like a page that still says Y.**

**And the same grep caught a FALSE CORRECTION of mine from six hours earlier.** «Adriana Crisci» is her baptismal name and I had «corrected» it to the civil form; «Arricole» is attested in the 1814 processetti and I had called it a spelling no document uses. **Both are amended on the entry that made them, not quietly dropped.**

**The mechanical check is the honest part.** Eighteen pairs, nine files, twenty hits — and the two it could not judge were exactly the two where a human had to open the source and look.

what: A plate caption quoted an act with three wrong numbers and the wrong date, under a title that repeated the date
was:
The plate **«A Falco stands for a Morgillo, on strada Camellara — 14 August 1843»**, captioned: «*Arienzo civil death register 1843, atto 33: «sono comparsi **GIUSEPPE FALCO, di anni cinquantacinque**, di professione COLONO … e **GIOVANNI CIOFFI, di anni quarantotto**, contadino … è morto nella sua propria casa **GENNARO MORGILLO, vedovo di Felicia Sompone***».

And the plate **«Giovanna Falco, aged seventy — 13 May 1832»**: «*her father was a different Michele Falco, married to **Vincenza Esposito**… She was born about **1762***».
now:
**4 AUGUST 1843.** **GIUSEPPE FALCO, di anni CINQUANTASEI.** **GIOVANNI CIOFFI, di anni QUARANTATRE.** **Felicia SANSONE.**

And **Giovanna Falco, aged SIXTY**, born about **1772**, daughter of Michele Falco and **VINCENZA SPOSITO**.
how: The site-wide drift grep found the retired surnames in `plates.json`; the numbers were then read off the images again. **The date needs no handwriting at all**: act 32 beside it is 3 August and act 35 is 10 August, so act 33 cannot be the fourteenth. The two ages were magnified — «*cinquantaſei*» and «*quarantatre*» — and «*ſeſſanta*» for Giovanna Falco carries two long **ſ** and no crossed **tt**.
why:
**A plate is a photograph of a document with the document's own words beside it.** It is the strongest thing this archive publishes and the least defended: the caption is prose, and prose is what the gates cannot read. **Four wrong numbers and a wrong date were sitting under two images of the acts that disprove them.**

**All of them had already been corrected in the data earlier today.** The corrections reached `households.json` and stopped there — the same failure as «Pivera», in the one place where the reader can see the original and check.

**One thing was deliberately NOT changed.** The parish Latin entry reads «*Mariae Angelae **ULIVIECCIO***» where the civil act reads «**MARIANGELA IULIUCCIO**». **Two sources, two spellings, and a Latin scribe is not a witness against an Italian clerk.** The household is named from the act and the parish form is recorded beside it — as «Adriana» and «Andreana» now are.

what: Francesca Falco married a CRISCI, not a Cioffi — and she has a second son
was: A household «**Gioacchino CIOFFI & Francesca Falco**», resting on **one document**: the death act of their son **ANIELLO**, seventy-six, of 27 July 1843. Her own death was recorded only as «**dead by 1843**».
now:
**GIOACCHINO CRISCI.** Both acts the household rests on were magnified on 20 September 2026 and **both read CRISCI** — a capital **C**, a narrow **r** shoulder, a long **ſ** with its descender, then **ci**. **No round o, which Cossi needs; no tall double-f ligature, which Cioffi needs.**

**And there is a second son.** «*è morto nella sua propria casa **LUCA CRISCI, di anni SESSANTA, marito di ANTONIA MORGILLO** … figlio di **GIOACCHINO CRISCI Defunto** … e di **FRANCESCA FALCO Defunta***» — Arienzo Morti 1829, **act 9, image 7 RIGHT**, died **16 January 1829**, born about **1769**.

**Both parents are «Defunto» and «Defunta» in that act**, so they died **before January 1829** — not merely before 1843.
how: Work-list row 80. The **1829 tavola alfabetica** produced the candidate while the indexes were being read for a different question entirely; **the act then produced the record.** The surname was then checked on the 1843 act as well — **which this archive had never magnified**, having taken the name from a transcription.
why:
**Three things change and one of them is a family.** Luca is **Aniello's brother**: seventy-six in 1843 gives about 1767, sixty in 1829 gives about 1769. **Two years apart, the same two parents.** The household goes from one document to two and from one child to two, and **Francesca Falco's death window closes by fourteen years.**

**And she married into the wrong family on this site for as long as it has existed.** A Falco woman marrying a **CRISCI** joins the surname the direct line married **twice** — Matteo Falco to Francesca Crisci, Vincenzo Falco to Andreana Crisci. **Nothing here joins her to either and none is claimed.** But the archive had her in the Cioffi, and the Cioffi are a different family on a different street.

**The order is the point.** The index gave a candidate whose surname it could not spell; the act gave the record. **A tavola may produce a candidate and never a record** — and this time the archive did it the right way round.

what: «Andreana CRISPI» was Crisci, and a surname that exists nowhere else came out of one letter
was: Sara Falco's birth act of 19 December 1828 quoted here as «*…è nata da **ANDREANA CRISPI**, di anni VENTISETTE, domiciliata in STRADA CAMELLARA*».
now: **ANDREANA CRISCI.** A capital **C**, a narrow **r** shoulder, an **i**, a long **ſ** with its descender, then **ci**. **A «p» needs a closed bowl to the right of its descender and there is none.**
how: Work-list row 58, act 118, image 122 left, magnified.
why:
**«Crispi» appears nowhere else in this archive**, and she is **Crisci** in every other act she is in — 1816, 1818, 1824, 1826, 1831, 1846, 1861, 1864. **One letter in one quotation invented a surname**, and it sat inside guillemets where it reads as the document's own word.

**Everything else in the act is exact, and one thing in it is the best age in the archive.** «*VINCENZO FALCO marito della stessa, di anni **TRENTASEI***» — thirty-six in December 1828, and **his baptism is 1 February 1792**. **The only stated age in this household's whole series that matches the register exactly.** The same office made him thirty-two in September 1826 and thirty-five in April 1816.

**And the mother declared the birth herself**, as she had in 1826, with the father named only as «marito della stessa».

what: Michele and Michelangelo Falco are two men — and they both married a woman called Antonia Vigliotti
was: An open question raised earlier on **20 September 2026**: whether **MICHELE FALCO**, forty-three in 1850, «*figlio di RAFFAELE FALCO defunto e di CHIARA RIVETTI defunta*», is the same man as **MICHELANGELO FALCO**, entered here as a son of **PASQUALE FALCO** and **CHIARA RIVETTI**, who married a **MARIANTONIA VIGLIOTTA** in December 1828. **Every discriminator between them had collapsed except a father's name that had never been read from an image.**
now:
**Both were read, and they are two men.** The 1828 marriage index, `an_ua14127` img2 act 10: «*10. **FALCO MICHELANGELO** | Arienzo | **FALCO PASQUALE, e RIVETTI CHIARA*** … ***VIGLIOTTI ANTONIA** | ivi | **VIGLIOTTI FRANCESCO, e REPETELLI VITTORIA*** … **Xbre 1828**». And the 1850 act's filiation, magnified for the first time: «*figlio di **RAFFAELE FALCO Defunto***» — a capital **R**.

**MICHELANGELO is a son of PASQUALE. MICHELE is a son of RAFFAELE.**
how: Work-list row 58, reading the tail of the citation list. **The 1828 index was cited on this site and had never been opened**; the 1850 father's name had been transcribed and never magnified.
why:
**And they both married an ANTONIA VIGLIOTTI.** That is not a misreading — it is two marriage records, and it is what had the two households tangled together for as long as this archive has held them.

**It unknots five children.** Michelangelo married Antonia Vigliotti in December 1828 and buried their daughter **Anna**, thirteen months, on **4 May 1831**; by **16 March 1834** he is the father of a second **Anna by RAFFAELA FALCO**. **So his Antonia died between 1831 and 1834 and he married again.** Michele's Antonia was still bearing children in 1834, 1836 and 1842 and he survived her in 1850. **Two women of one name, married to two men of almost one name, in one town.**

**MATTEO FALCO was standing in both households at once** — the act says MICHELE — and the row in the wrong one is left as a visible withdrawal rather than deleted. **That is how a child gets counted twice**, and it is the third time today this archive has found itself doing it.

**Her parents come free with the index**: **FRANCESCO VIGLIOTTI and VITTORIA REPETELLI**, neither of whom this archive held.

what: Her father is FRANCESCO Carfora — «VALERIO» was this archive's reading of the second half of a wrapped word
was: On **20 September 2026** this archive announced that a forename it had twice called illegible was not illegible but **split across a line break**, and published the resolution in capitals: «*The line ends «figlia di **Va**» and the next begins «**lerio** Carfora». **VALERIO** — and no other Italian forename ends in -lerio*». Maria Antonia Carfora's father went into the household file, the person pages and the research log as **VALERIO CARFORA**.
now:
**The wrapped word is «Fran-/cesco».** The line ends «*figlia di **Fran***» — an F with its crossbar, then r-a-n — and the next begins «***cesco** Carfora*», in which the third letter is this clerk's long *s*, not an r, and the fourth is a c, not an i; there is no dot anywhere in the fragment.

**But the letterforms are the weakest of the three proofs, and the other two need no handwriting judgement at all.**

**One.** The marriage act's own document list, item 6, is the bride's father's consent, «*dato nell'atto*». **The consent paper survives**, in the Arienzo processetti for 1860 — `an_ua14207`, bundle 3, image 33: «*L'anno milleottocentosessanta il giorno **primo Gennajo** in **Arienzo**. Innanzi a noi **Stefano Sargenti Sindaco** … si è presentato **FRANCESCO CARFORA**, contadino di detto comune, il quale presta il suo pieno consenso alla sua figlia **MARIA ANTONIA CARFORA** … contragga matrimonio col nominato **SABBATINO ANNECCHINO** fu **CARMINE**, e **ROSA CEGLIA**, contadino di **Forchia***». **The same official, the same town, three weeks earlier, writing the name unhurried and in full.**

**Two.** His daughter's birth act, found the same day: **Arienzo, Nati 1830, act 142, 30 December 1830** — «*è comparso **FRANCESCO CARFORA**, di anni ventotto, di professione contadino, domiciliato in questo Comune, strada **SIGNORINDICO***» — and again at the foot of the act, «*testimonj … da esso **Signor FRANCESCO CARFORA** prodotti*». **Twice in one act, in a clear hand.** His marriage of 29 June 1828 spells it a fourth time.
how: Work-list row 63. The 1828 Arienzo marriage tavola was read for a Carfora groom and gave **CARFORA FRANCESCO × MORGILLO PASQUA**; the act behind it was opened to check, and the couple matched the 1860 marriage act in everything except the father's forename. **That disagreement was treated as a problem with the archive's reading rather than with the find**, and the 1830 birth register and the 1860 processetti were opened to settle it. They settled it against the archive.
why:
**The argument that produced «Valerio» was better than the reading it defended, and that is what made it dangerous.** It was right that the word wrapped, right that the archive had magnified only half of it, right that half a word cannot be read. Then it completed the word by elimination — *no other Italian forename ends in -lerio* — and the elimination was sound while the four letters it ran on were wrong.

**Elimination over a misread fragment returns a confident answer, every time.** The fix is not to reason harder; it is to find the name somewhere the page is not folded. It was three weeks away, in the same town, in a document the act itself lists.

**What the old entry got right is kept.** The act does not mark him dead, and item 6 proves he consented in person: **Francesco Carfora, contadino of strada Signorindico, was alive at Arienzo on 21 January 1860.** Only the forename changes.

what: Two Carmine Annecchino of Forchia, and this archive held them under one name
was: **CARMINE ANNECCHINO** stood in two households at once: as the father of «Carmine Annecchino & Maria Carfora», whose children were born at Forchia between **1883 and 1901**, and as the grandfather of «Sabatino Annecchino & Mariantonia Carfora», named «*defunto*» in a marriage act of **1860**. The archive noted that no kinship was claimed between the two households, **but the two men shared one name string, so the person page merged them.**
now: **They are two men, and the proof is a date.** The 1860 marriage dossier holds Carmine Annecchino's death extract: **Forchia, Morti 1838, act 20, 8 August 1838** — fifty-two, colono of the **Masseria de' Preti**. **A man dead in 1838 did not father a child in 1901.** He is now **«Carmine Annecchino (of Antonio, d. 1838)»**; the other keeps the plain name.
how: Reading the 1860 Arienzo processetti (`an_ua14207`) for work-list row 77 — which this archive had recorded as blocked on ordering documents, and which is not blocked.
why: **The homonym rule this archive wrote after a living-people check nearly deleted a true fact says to resolve by identifier, not by name string.** It was written about the FamilySearch tree and never applied to the archive's own household file, where the same collision was sitting in plain sight — two men called Carmine Annecchino, in one town, forty-five years apart. **The rule was filed as a lesson about somebody else's data.**

what: Four readings on one line of the 1843 death register, all of them from the sweep, all of them wrong
was: Act 33 of the Arienzo death register for 1843 — the death of **GENNARO MORGILLO**, the most consequential single act in this archive's Morgillo work — was entered from a **triage sweep** and its row said: the act is of **14 August**; the first declarant is «**GIUSEPPE FALCO, di anni cinquantacinque**»; the second is «**Giovanni Cioffi**, 48, contadino»; and the dead man's wife is «**Felicia Sompone**». The file even recorded a puzzle the row created — a Giuseppe Falco who was «56 in May and 55 in August».
now:
**Read at 3,200 pixels on 21 September 2026, and four things change.**

**The act is of 4 AUGUST** — «*nel giorno **quattro** del mese di **Agosto** anno corrente, alle ore **diciassette***». The household file had 4 August all along; only the register carried the fourteenth.

**Giuseppe Falco is «di anni CINQUANTOTTO».** Fifty-eight, not fifty-five — **and the puzzle dissolves with it**: he was fifty-six in May and fifty-eight in August, which is a clerk rounding, not a man growing younger.

**The second declarant is NOT a Cioffi.** «*e **GIOVANNI CRIS[P/C]I**, di anni **quarantotto**, di professione contadino*». The surname's second letter is a zigzag **r**, not a round **o**, and there is **no double-f ascender** anywhere in the word: C-r-i, then a long descender, then a dotted i. **Whether it ends *-spi* or *-sci* is left open** — this archive has already been caught once treating that descender as decisive, in both directions.

**And «Felicia Sompone» was withdrawn a day earlier and never reached this file.** She is **FELICIA SANSONE**, and her daughter's birth act of 1822 spells it across a line break, «*MARIA FELICE **SAN=/SONE***».
how: Work-list row 73. The 1845 processetto was opened to prove that this act belongs to Crescenzo Falco's father-in-law; it does. Its certified copy of the act disagreed with the archive's own row about the date and the declarant's age, so the register was reopened at full resolution.
why:
**Every one of the four came from the same sweep, and the sweep was doing its job.** A triage band at low resolution finds the acts worth reading; it is not a reading. This archive has written that down — *the contact sheet is triage, and may produce a candidate, never a record* — and then left a swept row standing as the citation for the most important Morgillo act it holds, for a day, while a correction to one of its four fields sat published on this very page.

**The failure is not the misreading. It is that nothing re-read the act when the act became load-bearing.** A row promoted from triage to evidence should be re-read at that moment, and there is no gate that notices when one is.

what: Five fields wrong in one swept row — and it is the second act in an hour to fail the same way
was: Act 3 of the Arienzo death register for 1838, the death of **MARIA FELICE SANSONE**, was entered from a triage sweep. The row said she was **fifty-four**; that her father was «**Saverio Sansone**»; and that the two declarants were «**Salvatore d'Angelo(?)**, 42» and «**Gaspare Giglio(?)**, 60». The question marks were honest and the names were still published.
now:
**Read at 3,200 pixels. Five of the six fields move.**

**She is «di anni CINQUANTATRE»** — fifty-three.

**Her father is PASQUALE SANSONE**, not Saverio: the initial is a looped P with a descender, and the word is «*P-a-∫-quale*».

**The first declarant is SALVATORE SPOSITO**, not Salvatore d'Angelo.

**The second is CESARE DIGLIO**, not Gaspare Giglio — **and he is a man this archive already knows**: a **CESARE DIGLIO, forty-six, of strada Camellara** witnessed the birth of a Cioffi child on the same street in 1831. Forty-six in 1831 is fifty-three in 1838 and the act says sixty; *the street and the name are exact and the age is a clerk's guess.*

**Her mother survives roughly intact** — «*MARTA LE CASARO*» against the sweep's «Marta lo Casaro» — and even there the particle will not settle.

**THE SECOND DECLARANT IS THE HARD ONE AND THE DOUBT IS PUBLISHED WITH IT.** A **GASPARE GIGLIO, contadino of strada Camellara**, declares act 4 on the very next leaf, and acts 18 and 21 besides. **The two names are one stroke apart in this hand and the two men lived on the same street.** The reading here rests on the forename: «*Cesare*» has no descender between its letters and «*Gaspare*» must have one for its **p**. **The reading is claimed; the identification with the Cesare Diglio of 1831 is not.**
how: Work-list row 73. The 1845 marriage dossier carries a certified copy of this act, made in November 1844; the copy disagreed with the archive's row, so the register was reopened at full resolution. **The copy was wrong too**, on the mother's surname — it writes «LE CESA=/RE».
why:
**This is the second act in one hour to be found wrong in every field the sweep filled**, the other being Gennaro Morgillo's death in 1843. The two are husband and wife.

**The sweep is not at fault and neither is the reader.** A band at low resolution across a hundred and forty leaves is how this archive finds anything at all, and it is explicitly recorded here as triage. **What failed is that both rows were quietly promoted to evidence** — cited on person pages, reasoned from, built into a household — **without anyone re-opening the leaf at the moment they started carrying weight.**

**A row that came from a sweep should say so where it is used, not only where it was written.** It does not, and there is no gate that notices. That is now the oldest unfixed hole in this archive's tooling.

what: A household this archive created on Monday rests on a father's name that is wrong, and the record disproving it was already here
was: On **21 September 2026** this archive read act 20 of the Arienzo marriage register for 1854 — «*FRANCESCO FALCO, di anni **quarantotto** … figlio del **fu RAFFAELE** … e della **fu CHIARA RIVETTI** … **VEDOVO DI RAFFAELA FALCO***» — and, seeing the same parents in Michele Falco's act of 1850, created the household **«Raffaele Falco & Chiara Rivetti»** and gave it two sons. It was published with the note that the reading raised a question and settled nothing; **it still put a couple on this site who may never have existed.**
now:
**FRANCESCO FALCO OF 1854 IS FRANCESCANTONIO FALCO OF 1832, AND HIS FATHER WAS PASQUALE.**

Three records, all of them already in this archive on the day the household was made:

1. **6 July 1832**, read from the act: **RAFFAELA FALCO**, daughter of Giuseppe Falco and Antonia di Guida, marries **FRANCESCANTONIO FALCO**, «*figlio di **PASQUALE FALCO** … e di **CHIARA RIVETTI***», of **strada Camellara**.
2. **20 April 1854**, in the archive's own register: «***RAFFAELA FALCO, 34, contadina, strada CAMELLARA, MOGLIE DI FRANCESCO FALCO***», her parents **Giuseppe Falco and Antonia di Guida**.
3. **August 1854**, four months later: a **FRANCESCO FALCO** of **strada Camellara** marries again as «***VEDOVO DI RAFFAELA FALCO***».

**One Raffaela Falco, one widower, one street, four months apart.** And the same man is called **FRANCESCO** in his children's death acts of 1832, 1836 and 1838 and **FRANCESCANTONIO** in his marriage act and his son's birth act — *in the same registers, in the same years, by the same office*.

**So «figlio del fu RAFFAELE» is a clerk's error**, and the household built on it is left standing with this correction attached rather than quietly deleted.
how: Work-list row 87, running the cheapest test first: open Michelangelo Falco's own marriage act, which turned out to sit on the leaf after one this archive had opened five days earlier for a different family. That act says **PASQUALE**. Asking then what else the archive held about a **RAFFAELA FALCO** turned up her death act, cited on the register page since September, naming her husband.
why:
**The disproof was in the building the whole time.** Every one of the three records was already published here — one of them read from the image the day before, one cited on the register page for weeks. **What was missing was the question**, and the question was only asked because a work-list row forced the cheapest test to be run.

**And the same slip now sits under the other half of row 87.** Michele Falco's act of 1850 calls his father «RAFFAELE FALCO defunto»; the parish christened a son of Pasquale Falco and Chiara Rivetti **MICHELE ANGELO ANTONIO** in 1808; there is exactly **one** Chiara Rivetti death in fifty years of Arienzo registers and she is **«vedova di PASQUALE FALCO»**. **That is not yet proof and nothing has been merged** — but the correction of 20 September, which split Michele from Michelangelo on one magnified capital, is now the weaker of the two readings.
